532281|2026-06.headline: HCLTech Q1 FY27 revenue $3,650M, down 0.5% QoQ but up 2.6% YoY in constant currency; record Q1 net new TCV of $2.4B; FY27 guidance held at 1-4%.
532281|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was seasonally weak sequentially, with revenue down 0.5% QoQ and EBIT margin at 16.9% (up 39 bps QoQ, helped by lower restructuring). Services grew 3.5% YoY, with ITBS up 4.2% and ER&D up only 0.3% YoY after a 3.7% QoQ decline. Net new TCV of $2.4B was the highest ever Q1, excluding a mega deal signed in early July. Management kept FY27 organic guidance of 1-4% revenue and 17.5-18.5% margin, and announced entry into AI datacenters with an up to INR3,500 crore initial investment.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever Q1; excludes early-July mega deal
+4.5% QoQ; +6.9% YoY; INR64.25 including Labour Code one-time impact

segments.name: IT and business services
segments.commentary: Grew 4.2% YoY and was flat QoQ in constant currency, despite seasonal weakness and telecom client headwinds.

segments.name: Engineering and R&D services
segments.commentary: Grew 0.3% YoY but fell 3.7% QoQ, driven by Tech and Telecom and Media & Entertainment; management attributed it to discretionary cuts at two large US telcos and a high base in tech.

segments.name: HCL Software
segments.commentary: Revenue $313M, up 2.2% QoQ but down 5.3% YoY; ARR $1.063B, up 2% YoY. Jaspersoft acquisition completed in early July adds a visualization layer to the data portfolio.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic revenue growth guidance retained at 1% to 4% in constant currency; not raised despite strong Q1 bookings, as the band is broad and only one quarter has passed.
FY27 EBIT margin guidance retained at 17.5% to 18.5%, including approximately 40-50 bps of restructuring cost.
Guidance excludes acquisitions. Jaspersoft is expected to add roughly $10-15M per quarter of revenue from Q2 with seasonality; CTG acquisition expected to close later in Q2.
Mega deal (signed early July, Europe-headquartered Fortune Global 50 digital workplace) transition to start in a couple of months; steady state by April 2027; negligible FY27 revenue impact.
Management will revisit guidance after Q2 if directional change is warranted; macro view unchanged since March.
Medium-term FY28 margin guidance to be given with FY28 guidance next year; no medium-term margin band reiterated on this call.
capex_capacity: Initial investment of up to INR3,500 crore in an AI datacenter business, with potential to scale to 50 MW of capacity over the long term.

Investment to be staged and funded from free cash flow; possible funding via silicon/OEM partners, committed client capacity, hardware financing against contracted demand, and a mix of equity and debt.
Management in advanced discussions with clients to secure committed consumption from day one; part of capacity to be consumed internally in managed services and outcome-based contracts.
Strategic investment of $150M in Sarvam (Indian sovereign AI company) to build a full-stack sovereign AI platform for government and enterprises.
demand_pricing: Net new TCV $2.4B, highest ever Q1, well balanced across verticals, service lines and geographies; a Fortune 250 semiconductor equipment OEM signed for SAP-enabled design-to-manufacturing transformation.
Advanced AI revenue $171M, up 10.6% QoQ and 62.1% YoY. AI Force deployed across 92 client accounts.
Growth led by Public Services (+12% YoY) and Retail & CPG (+10.1% YoY); six of seven verticals grew YoY. Added one $100M client, six $50M, 11 $20M and 31 $10M clients YoY.
Geography YoY: USA +2.9%, Europe +0.1%, ROW +10.8%, India +16.9%.

BFSI growth attributed to AI-native approach and wallet share gains with top financial services clients; Life Sciences and Healthcare declined on lapse of medical device regulatory work and US healthcare stress.

Management sees divergence: AI-native and AI-amplified services growing strongly, AI-disrupted commoditized work being optimized further by automation. Revenue per employee up 3.3% YoY, rising for five consecutive quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What limits raising guidance given record Q1 bookings and the early-July mega deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the band is broad and only Q1 is done; the mega deal transitions over a couple of months with steady state only by April 2027 and negligible FY27 revenue impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the AI datacenter investment look like a colocation-cost build (about $7M per MW), and what further commitments follow?
qa_highlights.answer: INR3,500 crore is only an initial fraction of the long-term 50 MW plan; it is a full-stack play, not colocation, with further investment tied to free cash flow and funded via partners, client commitments, hardware financing, and equity/debt mix.

qa_highlights.question: Token costs: will they collapse or stay high, and what does that mean for services revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said token prices may fall but total token consumption will rise, so total cost rises; tiered architecture with enterprise SLMs creates a new engineering services wave in data work and training.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 18-19% soon, perhaps in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 margins were near 18% excluding restructuring; FY27 guidance is 17.5-18.5% including 40-50 bps restructuring; FY28 margin guidance will be given next year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ER&D decline and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Decline was in Tech and Telecom and Media & Entertainment, from sharp discretionary cuts at two large US telcos flagged last quarter, plus a high base in tech; no explicit outlook for further declines was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter datacenters now, and how does this differ from the cloud cycle? Also, what about GPU oversupply risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued private AI stacks and SLMs differ from the cloud cycle, that megawatts are an anchor and value lies in wrapped services, and that the market remains GPU-starved; no explicit utilisation or tenancy assumptions were given.

qa_highlights.question: Does the margin guidance include amortization from M&A, and is the services outlook tougher than at the start of the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is organic and excludes acquisitions including Jaspersoft and CTG; macro view is unchanged since March and management will revisit after Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How big will Jaspersoft be, and when does CTG close?
qa_highlights.answer: Jaspersoft is expected to add about $10-15M per quarter with seasonality, consolidated from Q2; CTG expected to close later in Q2.

risks_watch: Revenue guidance (1-4%) was held despite the strongest Q1 bookings; any Q2 change in tone is flagged by management as possible after Q2 results.
ERS revenue is under pressure from telecom and media discretionary cuts; further sequential declines are possible.
AI datacenter entry (INR3,500 crore initial, 50 MW long-term) carries capex, funding and utilisation risk; no committed-consumption figures or return metrics were disclosed.
Margin pressure from AI investment and restructuring (40-50 bps in FY27); FY28 margin view deferred.
Declining healthcare and life sciences revenue, with management attributing it to regulatory work ending and US healthcare stress.
Telecom client headwinds and a high-tech base effect; attrition 12.7% LTM and headcount down 3,292 QoQ.
Pending CTG acquisition closing and Jaspersoft integration; guidance excludes both.
532281|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on bookings, AI revenue growth and ROIC, but cautious on near-term services momentum: guidance was held rather than raised, with management citing a broad band and one quarter of data. Answers on datacenter economics and funding were detailed on strategy but light on quantified returns, utilisation or capex beyond the INR3,500 crore initial tranche.
key_quotes: Net new TCV booking for the quarter was $2.4 billion, highest ever Q1 bookings.
So we are not putting this entire investment in the balance sheet in a single year.
The guidance is organic growth guidance and does not include acquisitions including Jaspersoft.
Our strategy continues to be to deliver superior growth at stable margins.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is in advanced discussions with clients for committed consumption from day one and says investment will be staged and funded from free cash flow, with 50 MW long-term potential against an initial INR3,500 crore tranche; further tranches tied to commitments.

rows.label: Restructuring cost rolling off
rows.why: Restructuring cost was 62 bps in Q1 (EBIT 16.9% reported vs 17.5% ex-restructuring) and FY27 guidance includes 40-50 bps total, so the drag may ease as programs finish.

tone.note: Management was confident on record TCV, Advanced AI revenue (+62.1% YoY) and ROIC, but cautious on near-term services momentum and held guidance; analysts pushed on datacenter economics, utilisation and capex funding, and management gave strategy but few quantified returns.

532281|2026-09.headline: HCLTech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.3% QoQ to $3,724M and EBIT margin hit 18.2%, while FY27 revenue guidance was narrowed to 2.5%-4%.
532281|2026-09.overview: Services grew 3% QoQ and 4% YoY in constant currency, led by Advanced AI revenue of $219M (up 28.4% QoQ, 78% YoY). New bookings were $3.3B (up 27% YoY, 35% QoQ), the second-highest quarter ever. HCLSoftware revenue fell 5.8% QoQ and 11.2% YoY to $294M, though ARR rose 7.8% YoY to $1.134B (2.6% ex-Jaspersoft). EBIT margin was 18.2%, up 131 bps QoQ, and FY27 EBIT guidance of 17.5%-18.5% was maintained.

financial_highlights.change: +131 bps QoQ, +71 bps YoY; 19.0% adjusted for restructuring (84 bps)
LTM payout INR60, 88.6% of net income
+261 bps YoY; Services 49.4% (+411 bps), Software 19.2% (-264 bps)

segments.name: IT and Business Services (ITBS)
segments.commentary: Grew 2.7% QoQ and 4.4% YoY in constant currency. Growth was broad-based across verticals and geographies.

segments.name: Engineering and R&D Services (ERS)
segments.commentary: Grew 4.1% QoQ and 2.1% YoY in constant currency.

segments.name: HCLSoftware
segments.commentary: Revenue of $294M fell 5.8% QoQ and 11.2% YoY, mainly from fewer multiyear license renewals (multiyear subscription revenue $39M vs $81M in Q2 FY26). ARR grew 7.8% YoY to $1.134B.

guidance_outlook: FY27 company revenue growth (constant currency) guidance narrowed to 2.5%-4%, including 87 bps inorganic contribution; organic midpoint broadly unchanged.
FY27 Services revenue growth guidance 3%-4%, including 62 bps inorganic contribution.
FY27 EBIT margin guidance unchanged at 17.5%-18.5%.
Management expects Services to land slightly above the guidance midpoint; Q3 expected to be strong with a Software step-up.
Mega deal won in the quarter will not contribute revenue in Q3 or Q4; expected to start in Q1 FY28.
Management's desired medium-term EBIT band is 18%-19%, but it declined to commit to this given industry change.
capex_capacity: First AI data center planned in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, in partnership with Sarvam and the Government of Odisha.
Global Technology Center announced in Bhubaneswar; new Global Technology Center opened in GIFT City, Gujarat for financial services clients.
Advanced semiconductor lab launched in Bengaluru with an investment of INR185 crore (post-silicon engineering, testing, validation and failure analysis).
Completed acquisition of HPE's Telco Solutions Group (2 months consolidated in Q2, about $21M revenue); Jaspersoft fully consolidated (about $15M).
Announced intent to acquire Robotiq.ai, a Croatia-based enterprise RPA platform provider.
demand_pricing: Pipeline described as strong and balanced across service lines, verticals and geographies; healthy demand toward end of quarter, but management remains cautious given a fluid environment.
Large AI deals were largely single-sourced through partners; competition came mainly from boutique providers and from service providers in agentic AI build, semiconductors and inferencing.
Management said IP and platform revenue carries gross margins upwards of 70%; AI services margins are at least 7%-10% higher than traditional services.
Top-client buckets: +1 client in $100M+, +8 in $50M+, +10 in $20M+, +33 in $10M+ on a YoY basis. Three top-20 clients ramping down (two telcos, one manufacturer) were already factored into guidance.
Geographic growth YoY: USA +3.5%, Europe -0.3%, Rest of World +11.4%, India +21.8%. Retail and CPG +14% and Financial Services +7.1% led verticals; 5 of 7 verticals grew YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How is value shared between frontier AI labs and managed services, and how will it look in steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its value sits mainly in the FDE motion and services around OpenAI and Anthropic platforms, with a long tail of work once inside an enterprise. Pricing for some offerings includes token cost, making the economics non-linear rather than headcount-linked.

qa_highlights.question: Who is HCLTech competing with in Advanced AI deals?
qa_highlights.answer: The two largest AI deals were single-sourced via partners. Competition came from boutiques, and from service providers in agentic AI build, semiconductors and inferencing; IP platform monetization (e.g., AI Force line items) is now included in large deals.

qa_highlights.question: When will FCF-to-net-income conversion return to the 3-4 year average?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Shiv Walia said two one-time items (a bilateral advance pricing agreement tax payment and a contribution to an external gratuity trust) depressed LTM conversion; he expects it to revert to 100%+ as they roll out of LTM.

qa_highlights.question: Why not raise the top end of guidance given strong Services growth and a seasonally strong Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the environment remains volatile (citing the Middle East conflict) and it does not want to raise guidance; it expects Services slightly above the midpoint and a Q3 Software step-up.

qa_highlights.question: Are the AI engagements with OpenAI/Anthropic under T&M or fixed price, with meaningful TCV?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a mix: change management and operating model transformation engagements have some fixed-price deals, while agentic implementation on Google and similar platforms is largely time-and-materials.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ramp-downs in top-20 clients behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact from the three ramp-downs was already in guidance, though discretionary spend at the two telco clients could still weigh. Upselling to existing clients has kept the client buckets growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Software margin expand while revenue declines, and how do Services margins look?
qa_highlights.answer: Software Q1 had a one-off restructuring cost; excluding it, lower employee costs and lower amortization drove the QoQ margin gain. Services margins benefited from Project Ascend and the higher Advanced AI mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic decline in Software and how long can ARR-to-revenue disconnect last?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue fell about 15% YoY on an organic basis while ARR rose 2.6% ex-Jaspersoft. Management attributed the gap to upfront recognition of multiyear licences and perpetual licence timing, expecting renewals to return in FY28 and FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is there seasonality in HPE Telco Solutions (Aruba TS) revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only two months were consolidated and extrapolating to three months should be right; there may be small seasonality but nothing major.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q3-Q4 Services sequential growth expected to decelerate versus Q2 organic growth of about 2.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the mega deal not contributing until Q1 FY28 as the main outlier, and said it is being conservative given uncertainty, with Services likely above the midpoint.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from ecosystem partners, and what is the impact of frontier-lab partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not track partner-channel revenue reliably, much of it is influenced rather than direct. It is a small but growing professional services partner for hyperscalers and frontier and GPU companies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term margin range?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the earlier aspiration of 18%-19% remains the desired band, but he would not commit to it now, preferring to invest in capability and differentiation.

risks_watch: HCLSoftware: revenue declined 11.2% YoY; the gap to ARR growth depends on multiyear renewals returning in FY28-FY29.
Discretionary spending pressure at two telco top-20 clients, plus a steep budget-driven ramp-down at one manufacturing client.
Free cash flow conversion (LTM FCF to NI 87%) depressed by BAPA tax payment and gratuity trust funding; watch for reversion to 100%+.
Mega deal revenue begins only in Q1 FY28; H2 FY27 Services sequential growth looks slower than Q2.
Macro and geopolitical volatility (Middle East conflict cited) and US PERM program suspension (management says immaterial).
Limited disclosure of partner-channel and AI revenue split; AI pricing and token-cost pass-through economics still evolving.
532281|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on AI momentum, bookings and margins, but cautious on guidance: management declined to raise the top end, citing a volatile environment. Management was explicit in pushing investors toward ARR rather than reported Software revenue.
key_quotes: I think our value here is largely in the FDE motion, the services around it.
So we should be able to see that this FCI to NI revert to maybe 100% plus level as these one-off roll over from LTM calculation.
Excluding the impact of Jaspersoft, our ARR has grown 2.6% YoY despite a 15% YoY decline in revenue.
But 18% to 19% is our desired band, but I wouldn't want to kind of comment on it now, because the industry is changing significantly
We are seeing a good environment, and we hope it will continue. For Services, we feel confident to be slightly above the midpoint.

532285|2026-03.headline: Geojit's FY26 profit absorbed planned investments; distribution income up 10% and equity MF net inflow share rose to 0.40 from 0.33.
532285|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as the first year of "Geojit 2.0", a shift toward recurring income (mutual fund distribution, advisory, PMS, insurance) with investments in sales headcount, IT and brand. Net sales headcount rose by about 700 to 3,768, including 650 in sales, at a cost of about INR29 crores, and brand spend rose by about INR15 crores. Profitability was hit by these investments, with about INR54 crores of transformation expenses booked and ROE reduced as brokerage income fell. Management said the next two years would carry similar investment costs, and it stopped field hiring for the current year because of the West Asia conflict.

financial_highlights.metric: Equity MF net inflow market share
Transformation / investment expenses booked in FY26

financial_highlights.change: total cash about INR1,115 crores, of which INR700-800 crores already deployed in MTF and lending
PMS AUM grew about 8% YoY; INR450 crores in FY23
NRI income about INR90 crores in FY26

segments.commentary: Distribution income grew 10% in FY26 while brokerage income declined, which management cited as the reason for lower ROE. Legacy clients (7+ years) contribute 58-60% of broking and MF income.

segments.name: Insurance distribution

segments.name: Private Wealth

qa_highlights.question: How is the DIFC entity traction, and how does it differ from the existing Middle East JVs? What is the NRI AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: DIFC is a private banking external-asset-manager business that started operations in February 2026, with client onboarding expected by end-May 2026. Existing Middle East entities are retail-focused. NRI AUM is INR12,000-13,000 crores, with about INR90 crores of income in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Hiring and capex plans for the current year?
qa_highlights.answer: Field hiring has been stopped because of the West Asia crisis; only replacements will be made. IT spend of about INR30 crores is planned over three years.

qa_highlights.question: Buyback plans and borrowing to fund MTF, given cash of about INR1,100 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that borrowing is cheaper than using own cash and said it intends to borrow for MTF, LAS and NBFC needs. Buyback will be considered after SEBI rules are issued.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic client reaction in March and April?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said clients increased investments in MF, and that April was too early to judge given the ceasefire uncertainty. Management expects short-term apprehension but long-term industry growth.

qa_highlights.question: ROE trajectory and dilution from the strategic shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward ROE guidance. It said ROE fell because brokerage declined while distribution income rose; no equity raise is planned and the transformation will be funded internally.

qa_highlights.question: PMS growth is modest. What are the bottlenecks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PMS AUM grew about 8% YoY to INR1,450 crores and that the team has been selling PMS for only three years.

risks_watch: Profitability pressure from about two more years of investment costs, with ROE already lower because brokerage income fell.

532285|2026-06.headline: Geojit Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR160.4 crore and PAT to INR19.8 crore, but management guided to continued cost pressure and no hiring for several quarters.
532285|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR160.40 crore, up 11% YoY, with PBT of INR25.99 crore (up 4% QoQ) and PAT of INR19.83 crore (up 14% QoQ). Employee cost rose INR18 crore on sales force expansion, DIFC hiring, tech team additions and higher incentives, though management said employee cost would normalise after a lower insurance-incentive quarter. Customer assets reached INR1.11 lakh crore (up 15% QoQ), mostly from market appreciation, with recurring assets at INR26,000 crore. Management said margin benefits from FY26 investments would take a couple more quarters, and that hiring has been paused except for replacements due to Middle East conflict and market conditions. Leadership succession was also confirmed, with Jones George becoming MD from 1 October.

financial_highlights.change: Net inflows about INR2,000 crore over the year

financial_highlights.value: INR17,778 crore (as read in call; speaker first said INR1,778 crore)

financial_highlights.metric: Lending book (MTF and loan against shares)

financial_highlights.value: About INR1,000-1,100 crore; about 70% deployed in MTF/NBFC lending and trading, rest in FDs and AIF

segments.name: Broking
segments.commentary: Around 2 lakh active clients (one trade in last 12 months). Management said broking is not being neglected and that a significant part of tech investment will go to broking.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Over 3 lakh holding clients; equity MF net inflow market share improved to 0.473% and equity MF AUM is INR18,501 crore. About 38% of broking actives hold MF, leaving a 62% cross-sell gap.

segments.name: Insurance distribution
segments.commentary: Gross premium of INR103 crore in the quarter. Cross-sell penetration is under 5%, and growth is limited to existing clients.

segments.name: Asset management / PMS and AIF
segments.commentary: Asset management AUM about INR17,778 crore per the analyst's figure. Yield Plus AIF has run 11 months and is sold only to in-house clients so far; third-party distribution not yet appointed.

segments.name: GCC / NRI (Barjeel JVs, DIFC)
segments.commentary: GCC AUM is a little under USD 1 billion. Revenue is booked at share of JV profit (Barjeel 30%). Middle East business is under pressure since March, and expansion is paused. DIFC business only recently started booking.

guidance_outlook: Investments in technology and people to continue for about two more years.
Management expects margin and profitability benefits to show in coming quarters, not immediately; cost pressure to persist for the next couple of quarters.
Recruitment paused except for replacements until the geopolitical and market outlook is clearer; earlier plan had been aggressive hiring.
Branch breakeven takes 18-24 months; new employee breakeven 15-24 months for MF/trail-based sales (about 6 months for brokerage).
Buyback under consideration but no timeline; decision depends on other investment opportunities such as consolidation.
Jones George becomes MD of Geojit from 1 October; C.J. George steps down as MD; Satish Menon continues as MD of Geojit Investment Limited.
capex_capacity: Investment in technology is ongoing, with a new account opening module live in the trading app; the overall tech transformation aims for a single investment platform.
AI investment is in customer onboarding automation, research and portfolio analytics, and internal operations productivity; no quantified cost savings were given.
Branch network expansion is slowed; recruitment is limited to replacements.
Middle East expansion is on hold given the conflict.
demand_pricing: About 30,176 new clients added in the quarter, mostly through branch referrals with little from digital acquisition.
Industry SIP and new-client pace has slowed; management said market conditions influence SIP ramp-up.
Yield Plus AIF performed strongly over 11 months and has been sold only to in-house clients.
Middle East NRI business is under pressure from the conflict, and FCNR deposit rate increases and government encouragement of FCNR have also drawn inflows away.
Insurance income was lower in April-June than in Jan-Mar, reducing incentive outflows and employee cost.

qa_highlights.question: Are the FY26 investments starting to show up in financial performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some productivity gains are visible, but covering costs will take longer because most recurring MF, PMS and AIF revenue is trail-based.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall from the previous quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the March quarter carried high insurance incentive payouts, while April-June had lower insurance income, so employee cost normalised; fresh hiring is slow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East outlook and the GCC contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: GCC AUM is a little under USD 1 billion. Middle East investment decisions are on hold, and no expansion is planned until stability returns.

qa_highlights.question: What are the net cash levels and buyback plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash is about INR1,000-1,100 crore, with about 70% deployed in MTF/NBFC lending and trading. A buyback is being considered but has no timeline; consolidation opportunities may take priority.

qa_highlights.question: Why do investors choose Geojit given weak PAT over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Geojit focuses on delivery and MF trail income rather than F&O. It expects margins to improve in coming quarters, not immediately.

risks_watch: Profitability is still under pressure: employee cost is up INR18 crore and no near-term breakeven timeline was given for new hires.
SIP and new-client momentum has slowed, and productivity of the expanded sales force is still unproven.
Middle East and GCC NRI business faces conflict and FCNR-related outflows, with no expansion planned.
Customer asset growth was mostly market-driven, so flows need to be tracked against market moves.
Buyback and capital allocation remain undecided, with consolidation as a possible alternative use of cash.
532285|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on near-term profitability and hiring, but confident on the long-term recurring-revenue strategy. Management was evasive on the timing of a buyback and on margin visibility, and repeatedly said results would take a couple of quarters.
key_quotes: We believe the investment undertaken over the past year has created a stronger and more scalable platform positioning us well to benefit from the India's long-term financialization opportunity while creating sustainable value for our customers as well as our shareholders.
So, in my view, if the markets remaining like this in 2 quarters, we should be able to see good traction.
There is absolutely no question of neglecting broking, that's our important business segment.

rows.why: About 38% of broking actives hold MF, leaving a 62% cross-sell gap, and insurance penetration is under 5%, but growth is limited to existing clients and no targets were given.

rows.why: Cash is about INR1,000-1,100 crore with a buyback considered, but management gave no timeline and consolidation may take priority.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term recurring-revenue strategy and tech investment, but cautious on near-term profitability, hiring pause and buyback timing; analysts pressed on margin visibility, weak five-year PAT and why investors should choose Geojit over F&O-led peers.

532285|2026-09.headline: Geojit Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 2.5% YoY to INR 165.82 crores, but cost growth and weak cash-market broking kept profitability subdued.
532285|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 165.82 crores, up 2.5% YoY and 3.38% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR 36.7 crores and PBT of INR 20.62 crores. H1 revenue rose 6.72% while H1 EBITDA was INR 78.23 crores, with management attributing the margin pressure to higher employee and technology costs alongside subdued cash-market transaction income. Recurring revenue AUM rose to INR 26,737 crores in H1 from INR 23,230 crores at end-FY26, and asset management AUM (PMS plus AIF) grew 39% from March to INR 2,018 crores. Customer assets were broadly flat at INR 1.12 lakh crores as market correction in September offset inflows.

financial_highlights.change: Margin declined YoY per analyst question; exact YoY not stated

financial_highlights.metric: Recurring income share of total income (H1 FY27)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 735 crores a year earlier
vs INR 71 crores a year earlier; H1 INR 408 crores
Around INR 20,000 crores at end-August per management

financial_highlights.value: INR 156 crores monthly; about 1.78 lakh SIP clients

segments.name: Broking (cash and derivatives)
segments.commentary: Management said cash-market delivery volumes were subdued; derivatives are about 20% of total income and cash about 80%, of which about 90% is delivery. Transaction income is the main driver of EBITDA swings.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution / recurring
segments.commentary: MF AUM fell from about INR 20,000 crores at end-August to about INR 18,500 crores at end-September. 79% of MF income comes from clients with 5+ years of relationship.

segments.name: Asset management (PMS and AIF)
segments.commentary: PMS AUM about INR 1,770 crores (grown from INR 1,450 crores); Geojit Yield Plus Cat III AIF AUM INR 248 crores vs INR 22 crores a year earlier. Asset management income was INR 9.83 crores in Q2 and INR 18.4 crores in H1.

segments.name: Insurance
segments.commentary: Gross premium of INR 175 crores in Q2. Penetration is under 5% of clients for life and under 3% for health insurance.

segments.name: Lending
segments.commentary: Lending book of INR 780 crores, comprising margin trading facility and loan against shares and mutual funds.

segments.name: GCC / NRI and DIFC
segments.commentary: NRI business under pressure from FCNR deposit offers, rupee moves and GCC geopolitics; DIFC entity has about 50 relationships and about USD 2 million AUM booked, with revenue not yet meaningful.

guidance_outlook: No forward-looking numbers given on AUM from DIFC or Barjeel AMC in H2 FY27; management said DIFC is nascent.
Management expects EBITDA margin to stay subdued for the next one to two quarters if cash-market activity remains weak.
Priority is productivity of existing field force and cross-selling rather than headcount additions; new branch expansion is not aggressive.
Management intends to grow asset management aggressively, including empanelling third-party distributors, which may dilute EBITDA margin of that business.
Buyback or cash return to shareholders is under consideration, deferred pending possible strategic opportunities.
capex_capacity: Technology transformation is ongoing, replacing legacy systems and investing in cybersecurity; onboarding conversion speed improved about 15%.
Network of 529 offices at September-end vs 525 in Q1; new branch expansion described as not aggressive.
Employee benefit expense rose INR 8.17 crores YoY, driven by sales headcount, DIFC recruitment, IT team expansion and incentives.
Small investment planned in Bahrain; no other international investment planned at present.
demand_pricing: Gross inflows described as healthy, but September market correction (Sensex/market down about 6% in the month per management) offset flows; H1 net inflows about INR 1,400 crores, about 1.4% of customer assets.
Recurring income is percentage-of-AUM based, so management says a 6% market fall cuts income by about 6%, versus 30-40% volume drops in cash broking on a 6-7% market fall.
NRI/GCC business faces wait-and-watch sentiment and FCNR competition; management reported no major redemption pressure.
ARR inflows were said to be broad-based rather than driven by large tickets; PMS average client size is about INR 75 lakhs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cross-selling strategies given only a small share of clients hold multiple products?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20% of clients hold more than one product, mainly broking plus MF. Insurance penetration is under 5% for life and under 3% for health; MF is the first focus.

qa_highlights.question: Were Q2 ARR inflows of INR 322 crores driven by a few large tickets or broad-based?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflows were primarily broad-based, with a few high tickets. PMS average client size is about INR 75 lakhs on about INR 1,750 crores AUM.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the bottom-line decline despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman cited heavy technology transformation and cybersecurity spend, hiring of senior tech talent and field staff; market conditions weighed on transaction income. Hiring is expected to be muted going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the customer asset movement was MTM versus new inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 inflows of about INR 1,400 crores equal only about 1.4% of INR 1 lakh crore base; the flat customer asset level mainly reflects market valuation changes.

qa_highlights.question: How will headcount and employee cost be managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will be cautious and add staff only selectively, focusing on productivity of existing employees and reviewing cost per employee.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin improve and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin is tied to cash-market broking; management expects subdued margins for one to two quarters and cited historical 1-2 year lags before recovery.

risks_watch: Cash-market broking volumes remain weak; transaction income is a large part of EBITDA and margin recovery depends on market revival.
Cost base is rising (employee and IT spend) faster than revenue, so profitability growth may lag revenue growth.
NRI/GCC business is under pressure from FCNR deposit rates, currency depreciation and geopolitical uncertainty.
Capital allocation between technology, branches and shareholder returns (buyback) remains undecided.
DIFC and Barjeel AMC contribution is unquantified and not yet meaningful to revenue.
532285|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on long-term recurring-revenue strategy but cautious on near-term outlook; management repeatedly said H2 hiring will be muted and EBITDA margin subdued until capital market activity recovers. Management declined to give forward numbers on AUM, DIFC, or cross-sell targets.
key_quotes: So, this is not unexpected. Although today, with regard to hiring sales force, etcetera, it will be relatively muted going forward looking at the market situation as well as the emerging geopolitical situation.
Unlike the transaction-led brokerage business, a subdued market doesn't impact the recurring income so much.
Our main focus right now is to improve the productivity of the existing employees and having a close look at the cost incurred on these employees.

rows.why: Asset management net inflows were INR 322 crores in Q2 vs INR 71 crores a year earlier (H1 INR 408 crores), and management plans to empanel third-party distributors to grow the business aggressively.

rows.why: Employee benefit expense rose INR 8.17 crores YoY and management says H2 hiring will be muted and staff added selectively, which limits further cost growth pressure.

rows.why: Buyback or cash return is under consideration but deferred pending possible strategic opportunities, with no decision or size given.

532286|2026-03.headline: Jindal Steel Q4 FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,647 crores (INR 10,093/t) on ASP up INR 4,743/t QoQ, with FY27 sales guided at 10.5–11 Mt.
532286|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp sequential recovery: consolidated gross revenue rose 28% QoQ to INR 19,399 crores and adjusted EBITDA reached INR 2,647 crores, helped by a rise in HRC and TMT rebar prices and Angul volume ramp-up. Sales volume grew 15% QoQ to 2.62 Mt as the Angul expansion took steelmaking capacity to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa. A one-time impairment of INR 1,433 crores (standalone) and INR 834 crores (consolidated) was booked on the Australian WCL asset after the shaft was closed. Management said the major capex programme is essentially complete and the focus shifts to asset sweating and deleveraging.

segments.name: Steel (India, Angul/Raigarh/Patratu)
segments.commentary: FY26 production 9.25 Mt (+14% YoY) and sales 8.68 Mt (+9% YoY). Q4 production 2.65 Mt (+6% QoQ, +26% YoY) and sales 2.62 Mt (+15% QoQ, +23% YoY). Flat/long mix was 52:48 in Q4 and 49:51 for FY26.

segments.name: Raw materials / overseas mines
segments.commentary: Iron ore sourcing about 60% outside purchases and 40% captive, with pricing described as stable. Mozambique is EBITDA positive, South Africa operating but not EBITDA positive, and Australia is closed with minimal cash burn.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: 1,050 MW Shree Bhoomi power plant commissioned (two 525 MW modules); ramp-up to complete within H1 FY27. Surplus power to be sold but described as not material to financials.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at 11–11.5 Mt and sales at 10.5–11 Mt.
Q1 FY27 coking coal prices expected to rise by USD 20–25/t sequentially; iron ore movement of plus/minus INR 100–150/t per month.
Slurry pipeline (Barbil–Angul) to be commissioned in Q1 FY27; savings of about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps up.
Port facility to be commissioned; DRI-2 (2 Mtpa) expected towards end of FY27; PP2 also remaining.
Capex guidance of INR 7,500–10,000 crores for expansion and sustenance capex; remaining programme capex INR 11,545 crores.
Leverage expected to normalise by Q2 FY27; value-added flat mix expected to move from about 50% toward 70%.
Start-up costs of INR 125 crores in Q4 are said to be finished and not recurring.
capex_capacity: Steelmaking capacity raised to 15.6 Mtpa from 9.6 Mtpa after BOF2 and BOF3 (3 Mt each) at Angul; iron-making capacity increased by 6.6 Mt through BF2 (4.6 Mt, operational) and DRI2 (2 Mt, under construction).
Cold rolling complex of 1.2 Mtpa commissioned at Angul to support value-added product mix.
Coal pipe conveyor from Utkal C thermal coal mine to Angul is operational; slurry pipeline from Barbil to Angul close to completion.
Total planned capex programme INR 47,043 crores: INR 25,924 crores spent up to FY25 and INR 9,574 crores in FY26, leaving INR 11,545 crores.
Thakurani-A1 iron ore block declared preferred bidder; Saradhapur Jalatap East coal block awarded at end of last year.
Rail rake programme of about 79 rakes: 72 acquired, remainder expected within 2–3 months.
demand_pricing: Management expects India steel demand growth of about 9–9.5% and cites FY26 finished steel consumption of 164.2 Mt (+8% YoY) and Q4 consumption of 44.6 Mt (+10% QoQ).

Realisations lag because the order book mixes spot and contract sales; contracts priced at earlier levels still support Q1 realisations. Management said the market is holding firm despite a slight dip in recent weeks.
Management declined to give a Q1/Q2 realisation upside estimate, saying the market is hard to predict.
Flat sales focus is on infrastructure first, then building and construction, downstream products and automobiles. HSM grades developed for niche products are ramping in the current quarter.
Management said the Q4 sales run rate reflects seasonality, so no large sequential volume pickup is expected.
Safeguard duty on flat steel imports reduced to 11.5% from 12% effective 21 Apr 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will steel and realisation gains continue into Q1, and have contracts been reset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts on earlier prices continue and ASP rose strongly in Q4 because of the spot/contract lag; the market is holding firm, though slightly softer recently.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company shift to asset sweating rather than further capacity expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed the capex programme is essentially complete and the focus is on sweating assets, with INR 7,500–10,000 crores allocated to expansion and sustenance capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why is value-added share falling and what is the target mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the priority during ramp-up is utilisation, with mix optimisation starting in H1 FY27 and stabilising in H2. Flat mix is about 50:50 today and is expected to reach about 70% flat over time.

qa_highlights.question: What were the start-up costs this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Q4 start-up costs at INR 125 crores, most of which were booked in Q3, and said these will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the slurry pipeline savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said slurry savings are about INR 700/t of iron ore, or INR 750–1,000/t of steel as it ramps. Full utilisation is not expected this year, but per-tonne savings do not depend on utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further write-downs on overseas assets?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said no further write-downs are expected, based on an independent valuation. Australia has minimal cash outflow, and Mozambique is EBITDA positive.

qa_highlights.question: What are the raw material cost moves into Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Coking coal is expected to rise USD 20–25/t QoQ in Q1. Iron ore is expected to move by about plus/minus INR 100–150/t per month and is hard to predict.

risks_watch: Value-added product share fell to about 61% from 66% QoQ, and management says mix will move back toward normal levels only over time.
Coking coal cost increase of USD 20–25/t in Q1 FY27 could compress margins if steel prices soften; a dip in steel prices was acknowledged.
FY26 EBITDA per tonne fell to INR 10,482 from INR 11,712 in FY25 even as volume rose.
DRI-2 is due towards end FY27 and PP2 is also pending; slurry pipeline commissioning is due in Q1 FY27.
Leverage (1.66x net debt/EBITDA) is expected to normalise only by Q2 FY27.
Management gave no EBITDA margin or revenue guidance for FY27, only volume guidance.
Overseas mine EC capacity increase is pending with no date given.

532286|2026-06.headline: Jindal Steel Q1FY27 consolidated adjusted EBITDA INR 2,667 crore, INR 11,937/ton, with ASP up INR 7,500/ton despite 15% sequential volume drop.
532286|2026-06.overview: Q1FY27 revenue fell about 8% QoQ on a plant maintenance shutdown (BOF refractory change), with sales volume down 15% sequentially. ASP rose about INR 7,500/ton on stronger steel prices and richer mix, and value-added share rose from 61% to 66%. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 2,667 crore (INR 11,937/ton, up INR 1,843/ton), while PAT was INR 844 crore and finance cost rose to INR 548 crore as Q4FY26 expansion assets entered the P&L. Management guided to net debt/EBITDA below 1.5x in Q2FY27 (Q1: 1.71x) and a sequential cost recovery from the shutdown reversing, with the slurry pipeline targeted for commissioning around August.

segments.name: Flat products
segments.commentary: NSR moved about INR 7,000/ton QoQ higher per management. HRC prices were firm through the quarter, though management cited HRC down about INR 800/ton versus Q1 average in recent pricing.

segments.name: Long products
segments.commentary: NSR moved about INR 4,500/ton QoQ higher per Sandeep Modi. TMT rebar prices fell about INR 8,000 per index in recent weeks on monsoon seasonality, while rails, rounds, specialty angles and quench-and-tempered plates held prices.

guidance_outlook: FY27 sales volume guidance of 10.5-11 million tons maintained; management expects to recover about 300,000 tons of hot metal lost in Q1.
Q2FY27 cost structure expected to improve on no shutdown, operating leverage (about INR 2,000/ton in Q1) not repeating, and coking coal up a further $12-15/ton.
Slurry pipeline (18 MTPA design) expected to commission in first half of August, subject to monsoon; about INR 700/ton iron ore cost benefit from Q2 per management.
Cost reduction campaign targeting at least INR 1,000/ton, mainly electricity, fuel, coke, oxygen and yield (98% to 98.5%).
Angul blast furnace hot metal to ramp from 11,000 t/d to 12,000 t/d in September and 13,000 t/d by December.
Net debt/EBITDA expected below 1.5x in Q2FY27.
FY27 capex about INR 8,500 crore; about INR 2,000 crore spent in Q1. Ongoing capex envelope of INR 7,000-10,000 crore per year on value-added products.
capex_capacity: Cumulative expansion spend INR 37,457 crore of announced INR 47,043 crore; FY27 plan about INR 8,500 crore, about INR 2,000 crore spent in Q1.
Crude steel capacity installed 15.6 MTPA; FY27 output expected at about 11-11.5 MT, with 12.5 MT possible via blast furnace readjustment.
Angul: two blast furnaces (BF1 at 10,000 t/d rated, running about 11,000 t/d; BF2 rated 13,000 t/d), one DRI plant (5,000 t/d), EAF and BOF 1/2/3 (BOF 2 commissioned Sep-25, BOF 3 Mar-26).
Raigarh: two blast furnaces at 6,800 t/d combined (100% utilised), 10 DRI plants, three EAFs; Raigarh hot metal cited as 3.6 MT.
Slurry pipeline: 18 MTPA capacity, 60% Fe and 35-40% water; pellet plants of 6 MT existing plus 6 MT under addition, plus a 5 MT sinter plant, to absorb about 17-18 MT/year.
Plate capacity about 2 MT/year going to 2.5 MT; hot strip mill (commissioned FY24) rated 5-5.5 MT of HRC.
demand_pricing: Indian crude steel production down about 6% QoQ to 42 MT and finished steel consumption down about 7% to about 41.5 MT in Q1 on monsoon seasonality.
Management expects construction recovery from end-August after monsoon; HRC firm, TMT weak.
Imports of HRC via advance licences cited as a pressure on commodity flats; management says value-added grades are insulated.
Coking coal: $15/ton further increase expected; blend optimisation and coke imports from Indonesia cited as offsets.
Iron ore prices set largely by NMDC and OMC, which management treats as uncontrollable.
Share of high-EBITDA products targeted to rise; product EBITDA ranges from about INR 7,000 to INR 25,000/ton per management.

qa_highlights.question: What are the new management's key priorities and expansion plans at Angul?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities: utilise 15.6 MT capacity and shift mix to value-added grades; growth funded from earnings at INR 7,000-10,000 crore capex per year, with no commodity capacity additions and no new borrowing to expand.

qa_highlights.question: Current NSR movement and Q2 price outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Flats about INR 7,000/ton higher QoQ and longs about INR 4,500/ton higher QoQ; recent HRC about INR 800/ton lower and TMT about INR 8,000 lower, expected to recover post-monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 volume fall and what is the FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Shutdown was needed to replace BOF refractory after heat life of 9,000-10,000; about 300,000 tons of hot metal lost; FY27 volume guidance of 10.5-11 MT maintained.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of QoQ cost increase of about INR 5,500/ton?
qa_highlights.answer: Iron ore about INR 500/ton, Middle East conflict impact $12-13/ton, coking coal about $23/ton, and operating leverage from the shutdown about INR 2,000/ton.

qa_highlights.question: Quantified cost savings over next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets at least INR 1,000/ton cost reduction; slurry pipeline about INR 700/ton; Vishal Chandak pointed to 18-20% ROCE targets to back-calculate project EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA/ton not rising with value-added share?
qa_highlights.answer: Product-wise EBITDA is not disclosed; about 50% of portfolio is high-EBITDA, with aim to convert 1.5-2 MT of low-EBITDA volume to value-added.

qa_highlights.question: Concerns about frequent senior management changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said eight new board-level faces were brought in, including CFO, CHRO and VP HR; about 1,800-2,000 upper-middle managers are stable.

risks_watch: Long product (TMT) price correction and monsoon-driven demand weakness; timing of post-monsoon recovery.
Coking coal and Middle East-related input cost pressure, with $12-15/ton further coking coal increase expected in Q2.
Slurry pipeline commissioning slippage beyond August due to monsoon or trials.
Blast furnace ramp to 12,000 t/d in September and 13,000 t/d by December; Q1 rain-related electrical grid failure cited.
Net debt/EBITDA reaching below 1.5x in Q2FY27 from 1.71x.
Rising finance and depreciation costs from newly capitalised assets.
Jharkhand MoU (2.5-2.7 MT blast furnace) conditional on iron ore block allocation; no investment committed.
Senior management turnover, with eight new senior appointments.

Stronger steel prices and richer mix

rows.why: Q1 volume fell about 15% QoQ on the BOF refractory shutdown, about 300,000 t of hot metal is to be recovered, and operating leverage of about INR 2,000/ton does not repeat in Q2.

rows.why: Management expects construction to recover after the monsoon, but TMT prices are down about INR 8,000 per index in recent weeks and HRC imports via advance licences are pressuring flats.

532286|2026-09.headline: Jindal Steel posted record Q2 FY27 gross revenue of INR 19,448 crore (+44% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA of INR 2,504 crore (+34% YoY) on 2.38 MT sales.
532286|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly gross revenue of INR 19,448 crore and record sales volume of 2.38 million tons, with domestic sales about 92% of volume. Adjusted EBITDA rose 34% YoY to INR 2,504 crore, but adjusted EBITDA per ton of INR 10,529 was sequentially lower on higher raw material, power, fuel and freight costs. Net debt fell to INR 14,786 crore and net debt-to-EBITDA improved to 1.51x from 1.71x. Management guided to 11 MT gross steel output in FY27 with H2 net steel of about 6 MT, and said the switch from propane to coal-gas syngas protected productivity during the West Asia supply disruption.

financial_highlights.change: down INR 1,141 crore from INR 15,927 crore in Q1

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,228 crore in Q2; INR 3,187 crore in H1

financial_highlights.change: apples-to-apples basis; management says over 65% when excluding low-priced TMT

segments.name: Flat products (HRC and plates)
segments.commentary: Plates production exceeds 220,000 tons per month across both locations; management targets a 65:35 flat-to-long mix, up from about 60:40 currently. Hot-rolled coil output is being shifted to value-added grades such as high and medium carbon.

segments.name: TMT / long products
segments.commentary: TMT output was cut to about 120,000 tons per month from 220,000 tons earlier, with volume redirected to plates and HRC. TMT now goes mainly to major projects.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports run at about 100,000 tons per month, mainly HRC, plates, with some rails and structurals.

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: Pellet output is about 33,000 tons per day (Barbil 18,000-20,000 and Angul 14,000), all consumed in-house. A new pellet plant is targeted for commercial production by June 2027.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: JSOL (100% subsidiary) turnover and EBITDA are rising as major projects commission; Mozambique coal EBITDA improved YoY on better coal prices.

guidance_outlook: Net steel production target of about 6 MT in H2 FY27 (about 3 MT per quarter, planned at 0.96 MT per month); gross steel about 11 MT for FY27.
Record production expected in Q3 FY27 (Oct-Dec 2026), with Q4 to exceed Q3.
FY27 sales volume guidance lower end of about 10.5 MT; management says 9-9.5 lakh saleable tons per month is needed and that they are comfortable.
Coking coal cost increase of USD 20-25/ton expected for Q3; a possible further USD 20/ton from diesel and oil if the West Asia conflict prolongs.
Slurry pipeline (192 km, Barbil to Angul) commissioned; commercial supply from about 2-3 days from 23 Oct, saving about INR 700/ton on freight at 20,000 tons per day.
Blast furnace at Angul (about 10,000 tons per day) to ramp to 10,500 in about 7 days, 11,000 in November and 12,000 in December.
Coal gasifier expansion (3 more gasifiers, 35,000 NM3/hr each) and DRI-2 (2 MT) targeted for commissioning by June 2027.
Utkal B2 coal mine clearance expected in FY27; Roida iron ore mine restart expected by about December 2026 to January 2027.
Annual growth capex guided at INR 7,500-10,000 crore; net debt-to-EBITDA to stay below 1.5x through the cycle.
capex_capacity: Blast furnace at Angul ramping to about 10,000 tons per day, targeting 12,000 tons per day by December 2026.
Slurry pipeline: 192 km, commissioned, first iron slurry dispatched, continuous operation planned.
Captive coal mines: about 15 MT total capacity across Raigarh and Angul; captive coal meets about 50-55% of requirement, targeted at 65-70%. Gare Palma about 4 MT.
Kasia iron ore mine at 22,000 tons per day, ramping to 30,000 tons per day.
Coal gasification: 3 additional gasifiers (105,000 NM3/hr combined), over 95% indigenous content, commissioning by June 2027.
Total capex plan of about INR 47,000 crore with INR 8,000-9,000 crore remaining, including DRI-2 and performance-linked payments.
demand_pricing: Average HRC moved from INR 51,000 to INR 60,000/ton during Q2; TMT from INR 52,000 to INR 59,000/ton; structurals INR 60,000-65,000; rails above INR 70,000.
Spot prices around INR 60,000/ton for HRC and TMT as of late October.
Coking coal cost rose about USD 12-15/ton in Q2, within prior guidance; management says prices are stable now.
Propane to coal-gas switch saves about INR 70/kg in reheating furnaces (propane about INR 100/kg vs syngas about INR 30/kg). Management says the company will not revert to propane.
Q2 is seasonally weak for TMT; Q3 expected to be stronger on festive-season construction demand.
Europe steel deficit of about 28 MT cited; EU CBAM and quota remain open issues for exports.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4.8 MT H1 production run-rate achievable and will flat mix stay at 70:30 in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of about 3 MT per quarter; mix target is 65:35 flat to long, not 70:30, to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How much freight saving does the slurry pipeline give, and any extra cost?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 700/ton on freight with no additional cost; around 500 of 700 daily iron ore trucks to be removed.

qa_highlights.question: Coking coal and West Asia cost impact for Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Coking coal up USD 20-25/ton expected in Q3 by Sandeep Modi; West Asia impact on fuel about USD 4-5/ton, steady. Another USD 20/ton possible if conflict prolongs.

qa_highlights.question: Water availability from Brahmani for Angul at higher volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Only 31 MLD being used against 59.1 MLD sanctioned; usage to fall at least 15% next year as Barbil slurry supplies water.

qa_highlights.question: Power sales and their EBITDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said power sales are miniscule relative to the INR 1 lakh crore revenue ambition; no figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Pellet plant and merchant pellet sales?
qa_highlights.answer: No merchant pellet sales now; all 33,000 tons/day consumed in-house. New pellet plant commercial production by June 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Realisation and spot price detail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined exact spot prices, citing policy; gave approximate ranges as above.

risks_watch: Coking coal and diesel cost pressure from the West Asia and Russia-Ukraine supply disruptions; management flagged possible USD 20-25/ton in Q3.
Execution on the Angul blast furnace ramp, Roida mine right-of-way, and Utkal B2 approvals.
Possible delays to DRI-2 and coal gasifiers, which management says could slip from June 2027 due to imported equipment.
Other expenses rose about 13% QoQ on freight and power/fuel; management expects normalisation in Q3.
Water availability at Angul given the Brahmani river reservoir level, though management says consumption will be lower.
EU quota and CBAM outcomes that determine export access.

532296|2026-06.headline: Glenmark Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23.1% YoY to INR40,185 million; base business growth was above 18% excluding ISB 2001 deferred income.
532296|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR40,185 million, up 23.1% YoY from INR32,644 million, with North America (+41.1%, or +19.8% core excluding ISB 2001 deferred out-licensing income) and emerging markets (+27.7%) the main drivers. India formulations grew 15.5% to INR14,321 million, outgrowing IPM by about 6 points in Q1 per IQVIA. Europe was muted at +11.9% as management shifts the mix toward branded respiratory and dermatology products. Management said gross margin was held despite higher API, packing and logistics costs linked to the geopolitical situation, and reiterated a 21-22% full-year margin guide.

financial_highlights.metric: Base business growth excluding ISB 2001 deferred income

financial_highlights.change: +41.1% YoY; +19.8% core excluding ISB 2001 deferred income
Guided at 7-8% of revenue going forward; management said Q1 was a bit lower
Management said cash only; gross debt zero maintained

segments.name: India formulations
segments.commentary: INR14,321 million, +15.5% YoY; +18.1% in Q1 and +14.3% MAT June per IQVIA vs IPM at 12.2% and 10%. Ranked 13th with 2.37% share; 11 brands in IPM top 300.

segments.name: India Consumer Care (GCC)
segments.commentary: Primary sales INR1,558 million, +28% YoY. Candid grew over 30% across variants; LA SHIELD mid-single digit; Scalpe and Bontress grew very strongly.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: INR10,974 million, +41.1% YoY; +19.8% core excluding ISB 2001 deferred income. Nine products launched in the quarter; RYALTRIS US commercialisation started; fluticasone 44 mcg first ANDA approval with 180-day CGT exclusivity.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: INR7,472 million, +11.9% YoY. Branded portfolio grew well; RYALTRIS gaining share via Menarini; WINLEVI launched in UK, Nordics, CEE, Spain and Portugal. Management guides high single-digit FY27 growth and double-digit from FY28.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: INR7,304 million, +27.7% YoY. Russia secondary sales grew 12-plus% (IQVIA MAT May 2026); APAC double-digit secondary growth; RYALTRIS launch in Brazil planned for H2 FY27.

segments.commentary: Marketing applications in more than 90 countries; commercialised in 57 markets with 10 more expected over coming quarters; global secondary sales growth upwards of 40% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: R&D spend for the quarter and incremental spend after ISB 2301 moves to clinic?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D was about INR289 crore in Q1, a bit lower than run-rate; guidance is 7-8% of revenue. IGI burn is about INR70 million, covering 2301 Phase I and trials over the next 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in Europe, and what share of Europe sales is branded?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe is expected to finish FY27 at high single-digit growth after four years of fastest growth; branded is about 30% of Europe revenue today, targeted at about 60% over five years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US injectables contribution meaningful yet?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet meaningful; most injectables are commodity products. US growth this year is driven by respiratory launches (fluticasone 44, OTC nasal spray), with Monroe differentiated injectables contributing next year.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin impact from war-related API and logistics costs, and FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Pressure is on API, packing and logistics; mitigation through product and geographic mix. Pressure may persist for at least two more quarters; full-year 21-22% margin guide retained. No quantified bps impact given.

qa_highlights.question: Will India secondary-sales convergence persist and how should India be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India can be modelled at 12-15% consistent growth; cardiovascular growing about 15%, chronic respiratory above 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital, net cash and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital well below the 115-day full-year guide; gross debt zero maintained; operating cash of INR800-900 crore. Management declined to give a precise net cash figure.

qa_highlights.question: Status of US respiratory ANDA approvals and BioCryst ISB 830 agreement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes at least two of three H2 respiratory approvals (110 mcg, nasal spray Rx, ipratropium) come through. ISB 830 backup STAR-0310 has completed Phase I; BioCryst next steps unclear after its Astria acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Status of AbbVie (ISB 2001) payments received?

532296|2026-09.headline: Glenmark Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue flat at INR473 million reported, but like-for-like growth near 20%; H1 cash flow negative on INR520 million litigation payouts and field force build-out.

Management said the H1 margin dip reflects front-loaded oncology field force hiring (about 1,100 people) and litigation settlements, and expects operating leverage in H2; gross debt is guided to zero by end FY27.

532300|2026-03.headline: Wockhardt FY26 revenue INR3,373 crore, EBITDA about INR630 crore (~51% growth); Zaynich US FDA approval is the key catalyst, with peak sales guided at $1.5-2 billion globally.
532300|2026-03.overview: Management hosted an investor meet on 4 June 2026 (disclosed 11 June) after the US FDA approval of Zaynich (cefepime-zidebactam), described as the first Indian-discovered research product approved by the FDA. FY26 revenue was INR3,373 crore, EBITDA about INR630 crore (margin about 18.6%, up from about 5.4% three years earlier) and profit before tax INR238 crore. Management framed the next phase as scaling growth: US launch of Zaynich via an operationally light model, India and emerging-market launches, and biosimilar diabetes expansion. Most numbers were given verbally; no quarterly figures or formal guidance were disclosed in the presentation.

segments.name: Pharma core (India, UK, Ireland)
segments.commentary: About 75% of business; UK is top-five with 18% covered-market share and focuses on specialty injectables. India driven by diabetes, orthopedics, pain and regenerative medicine (Emrok, Miqnaf).

segments.name: Biosimilars / biotech (diabetes)
segments.commentary: Grew 27% in FY26; human insulin output scaled 2x and glargine 1.5x. Two products commercialised, five in pipeline (aspart, RN 30/70, degludec, degludec aspart, semaglutide); registered in 30 emerging markets.

segments.name: Novel antibiotics (Zaynich, Emrok, Miqnaf, Odrate)
segments.commentary: Specialty (biosimilars plus novel antibiotics) is 23% of business. Zaynich has US FDA and CDSCO India approvals; US launch planned with leadership hired and a commercial operating partner; European approval expected by end of calendar 2026.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: 28% of turnover, growing 35%, supported by partnerships in Brazil, Thailand, Algeria and Malaysia. Plans to launch Zaynich in seven to eight high-carbapenem-resistance markets within 18 to 24 months.

Revenue ramp expected to be slow initially (hockey-stick pattern), with breakeven in 12 to 18 months in the Zaynich business; first 12-18 months may see a slight loss, per the Chairman.
Zaynich US price expected at roughly $1,200-1,500 per day, with India pricing about 75-80% below US; Europe and US pricing described as price-neutral versus existing antibiotics.
Long-term target of about 20-25% share of resistant cases globally; India possibly higher.

capex_capacity: Planned capex of INR200-300 crore over the next three years, mainly for biologicals capacity.

Zaynich manufacturing: US supply from an FDA-approved European site; India supply from Indian facility; emerging markets to be supplied from either India or Europe depending on timelines (Europe could save six to nine months).
Company has 11 manufacturing facilities and two R&D centres in-house.
Management said US, Europe and emerging markets filings are submitted or in progress, with European approval expected by end of 2026.
demand_pricing: US cUTI is the largest of about 1.2 million US gram-negative hospital infections (about 600,000 cUTI cases); management cited about 20-25% readmission rate for cUTI.
India: about 600,000-700,000 gram-negative infection patients, with 35-45% estimated carbapenem resistance (ICMR surveillance caveated by regional variation).
Phase 3 vs meropenem: composite cure rate 96.8%, about 20% higher than meropenem per management.
Management said new anti-infectives in the US market total about $1 billion; the company does not plan to create new demand but to take share, with price neutrality.
Competition: cefiderocol (Fetroja) cited as the closest competitor; management claimed Zaynich has a better efficacy and safety profile, without numerical head-to-head data.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue from Zaynich over the next 6 to 24 months, and capex and commercial costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman expects slow initial revenue growth, a hockey-stick curve after 12-18 months, INR200-300 crore capex over three years, and no capex for sales build-out, only revenue cost. Breakeven expected in 12-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Does Zaynich qualify for the 10% PLI and what is the China strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Government funding recognised but immaterial versus R&D spend. China: Chinese patients in trial were insufficient; a small China study is ongoing and a partner may be sought.

qa_highlights.question: Will Zaynich be made in Europe for the US and in India for emerging markets?
qa_highlights.answer: US supply from an FDA-inspected European site as a de-risking step; India supply from India; emerging markets from India or Europe depending on timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Wockhardt exit US generics and will it re-enter?
qa_highlights.answer: US generics were about 5% of the portfolio and loss-making, amid the 2012-13 FDA import alert. Management said it is re-entering with innovative products sourced from European manufacturers, with India production for India.

qa_highlights.question: Patent life and exclusivity for Zaynich, Emrok and Miqnaf?
qa_highlights.answer: Zaynich patent runs to 2038 in India with further filings planned; Miqnaf patent to early 2033 in India. QIDP status gives five extra years in US; minimum 10-year market exclusivity in US and Western markets.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing and patient targets for FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: US price about $1,200-1,500 per day, typically $10,000-15,000 per course; India priced about 75-80% below US. Long-term share of 20-25% of resistant cases, with no FY28-29 patient numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Peak sales of Zaynich?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $1.5-2 billion per year globally at peak, not cumulative, with US around 40% of global revenue.

532305|2026-06.headline: Ind-Swift Q1 FY27 operating EBITDA rose 2.85x YoY to ₹33.32 crore, a 17.91% margin, with management guiding to 20%+ from Q3.
532305|2026-06.overview: Operating income grew 21.16% YoY to ₹186.08 crore and operating EBITDA reached ₹33.32 crore (17.91% margin, up 1258 bps). PAT excluding exceptional items was ₹24.68 crore (13.26% margin vs 4.99%). Management attributed the step-up to exit of litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business after the merger, and to a higher own-brand export mix. CDMO contracts with Viatris, Manx and Arrotex were commercialised in the quarter but contributed only about ₹5-6 crore so far, with ramp-up expected from Q2 and Q3. Management reiterated FY27 export sales of about ₹750 crore and ₹1200 crore revenue by FY29, and declined to revise targets at this stage.

segments.name: Export own-brands
segments.commentary: 57.20% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 48% in Q1 FY26; management cites this mix shift as a key margin driver. Export gross margin was stated at about 55%.

segments.name: Export contract manufacturing (CDMO)
segments.commentary: 26.64% of Q1 FY27 sales versus 29% a year earlier. Viatris, Manx and Arrotex partnerships commercialised in the quarter, with about ₹5-6 crore booked from Viatris products (Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules) so far.

segments.name: Domestic segments
segments.commentary: Branded generics 6.41%, ethical 6.14% and domestic contract manufacturing 3.61% of Q1 FY27 sales, all lower than a year ago. Management describes these as a stable cash-generation base; domestic sales are seasonal.

segments.name: Product portfolio
segments.commentary: Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin was about ₹25 crore in Q1 FY27 per management, partnered with Tiffen-Becker. FY26 revenue: Atorvastatin ₹85.50 crore, Ezetimibe + Atorvastatin ₹80.78 crore, Fexofenadine ₹74.32 crore, Quetiapine ₹19.75 crore, Famciclovir ₹18.64 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 export sales target of about ₹750 crore, with roughly 45% from CDMO (per management).

FY29 revenue target of ₹1200 crore; management said it is not revising this yet and will revisit by year-end. Mentioned FY27 expectation of about ₹900 crore and a longer-term aspiration of ₹1500 crore revenue and ~₹200 crore net profit by FY30.
EBITDA margin of 18% described as sustainable; management expects to move above 20% from Q3 FY27 (Q2 internally targeted), potentially 21-22% with sequential sales growth.
Viatris CDMO volumes expected to double in Q2 versus Q1; Arrotex Macrogol push expected in Q2, and Ibuprofen and Clarithromycin granules to contribute in Q3-Q4.

Samba facility upgrade to EU-GMP and PIC/S standards in progress as planned.
Capacity utilisation for Ibuprofen and granules about 70% in Q1 per management; management expects 90% utilisation of planned FY29 capacity over time.
Capex for a potential new CDMO customer deal estimated at ₹50-75 crore, with revenue of ₹150+ crore expected.
R&D working on 5-6 molecules for FY27-29; capex to follow only after filings are completed. New R&D land bought in Panchkula area.

qa_highlights.question: What are export margins for CDMO and own-brands, and how will the ₹250 crore cash and Synthimed stake be used?

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18% EBITDA margin sustainable, and could it rise further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 18% is fully sustainable and could reach 21-22% if sales grow quarter on quarter. It denied calling Q1 a turnaround, citing litigation and other costs borne by the formulation business for about 1.5 years that are now over.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY29 revenue guidance of ₹1200 crore not being raised, and when does growth come?

qa_highlights.question: Why was the API business sold and what R&D capability was retained?

qa_highlights.question: What is capacity utilisation and will there be a capacity shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Ibuprofen and granules ran at about 70% in Q1 on pilot batches. Management expects 90% utilisation of the FY29 plan over time and sees no capacity dearth. Capex for new molecules will follow only after filings are complete.

532305|2026-09.headline: Ind-Swift Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 50.15% YoY to ₹234.89 crore, with operating EBITDA margin at 18.02% and PAT of ₹31.03 crore.

532309|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 PBT from continuing operations hit INR 119 crore, but one-offs (incl. ~INR 44 crore BHEL ECL reversal) drove much of it; underlying FY26 EBITDA margin 11%.
532309|2026-03.overview: GE Power India reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 316 crore (up from INR 266 crore YoY) and FY26 revenue of INR 1,269 crore (up 21%), led by Core Services (+14%) and Upgrades (+24%). Profit before tax and exceptional items from continuing operations was INR 119 crore in Q4 versus a loss of INR 15 crore a year earlier, and INR 340 crore for FY26 versus INR 22 crore, with management flagging sizeable one-offs in both periods. Order intake fell sharply to INR 877 crore for FY26 from INR 2,183 crore, and order backlog declined to INR 1,628 crore from INR 2,662 crore, mainly due to termination of FGD-EP contracts. Management is pushing a service-led, short-cycle strategy, has settled with BHEL and Jaypee, and has signed a Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy, with a recommended dividend of INR 7 per share (70% of face value).

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 14% YoY and core orders rose 32% YoY; Core Services order backlog up about 40% YoY. Management says about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book executes in FY27 (12-month cycles).

segments.name: Upgrades
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 24% YoY, driven by upgrade volumes in Q4; Vindhyachal and Wanakbori complex upgrade orders of INR 591 crore were booked in FY25.

segments.name: New Build / FGD EPC (AQCS)
segments.commentary: In close-out mode; FGD-EP contracts of Jaypee Bina and Nigrie (INR 775 crore) were terminated, driving backlog decline. Seven operational acceptances and four unit completions achieved in FY26.

segments.name: Durgapur manufacturing (discontinued)
segments.commentary: Being demerged to JSW Energy; asset of about 660 acres, reported losses in recent quarters. Five-year JSW supply and capacity agreement signed to protect core services manufacturing needs.

qa_highlights.question: Of the order book, how much is executable in FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Will backlog grow after the current book runs off, and is the business widening beyond core?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is new-build close-out. Core backlog is up about 40% YoY; the company plans to grow its 18% share of the INR 3,500-4,000 crore fleet before expanding to other areas.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 450 crore loan and what yield does it earn?

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the FGD opportunity and the margin range?

532331|2026-09.headline: Ajanta Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% to Rs 1,794 crore and PAT 49% to Rs 388 crore, but management guided to a weaker H2 on US and institutional normalisation.
532331|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 33% to Rs 1,794 crore, EBITDA rose 47% to Rs 543 crore (30% margin) and PAT rose 49% to Rs 388 crore. Every business grew in the quarter, led by US generics (+41%), Africa branded generics (+41%) and Africa Institution (+259%), with Asia branded generics rebounding 18%. Management said H1 benefited from elevated US sales on a limited-competition product and an unusually strong institutional quarter, both of which will normalise in H2. FY27 guidance was retained at high-teens revenue growth, around 27% EBITDA margin and around 78% gross margin, with US growth guidance cut to high single digits from mid single digits.

532341|2026-03.headline: IZMO Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue hit a record INR109.16 crore (+82.5% YoY), with FY26 revenue up 26.8% to INR284.88 crore.

FY26 consolidated net profit was INR47.56 crore, broadly flat YoY, which management tied to izmoMicro investment-phase costs. Management guided FY27 izmoMicro revenue to INR45-50 crore, EBITDA margin to 20-25%, and said it is raising about INR150 crore (equity-cum-debt, not yet finalised) mainly for capex.

532343|2026-03.headline: TVS Motor FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 47,270 crores with record Q4 revenue of INR 12,808 crores and 13.1% EBITDA margin.

Q4 revenue of INR 12,808 crores grew 36% YoY with EBITDA margin of 13.1%, against 6.5% when the margin recovery began. qa_highlights.question: What commodity inflation and price increases are expected in Q1 and Q4?

qa_highlights.question: What are current 2W and 3W production capacities and the planned additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is being increased by 1.5 million units to about 8.3 million. Management said this is the first significant addition in 12 months, and capacity will not constrain growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where are supply-chain constraints (raw materials, labour, rare earths) and channel stock?
qa_highlights.answer: Constraints are energy/gas, Tier 2 labour shortages and raw material timing. May is better than April, and channel stock should normalise by end-May or early June. Q4 international revenue was INR 2,999 crores and spare parts INR 1,122 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management cautious for the next two quarters, and what are the risks to demand?

qa_highlights.answer: EV output is about 40,000 units per month, moving toward 50,000. Asian markets are taking a growing share of EV volumes, with iQube and Orbiter launched there.

532343|2026-06.headline: TVS Motor Q1 FY27 revenue rose 38% to INR 13,896 crore and operating EBITDA rose 41% to INR 1,779 crore, with margin at 12.8%.
532343|2026-06.overview: Total volume grew 28% YoY to 1.63 million units, with revenue of INR 13,896 crore (+38%) and PAT of INR 1,174 crore (+51%). Operating EBITDA margin expanded 30 bps to 12.8%, helped by price increases and cost actions despite a sharp commodity spike linked to the West Asia conflict. International sales hit a record 4.68 lakh units (+33%), and EV sales grew 86%. Management guided Q2 as better than Q1 and expects FY27 industry growth in double digits, with capacity expansion to 8.3 million 2W units by Q4.

segments.name: 2-wheeler international
segments.commentary: International market ICE sales grew 31%. Africa, Asia and LATAM contributed, with HLX crossing 5 million cumulative units.

segments.name: 3-wheeler
segments.commentary: Total sales rose 48% to 67,000 units from 45,000 units.

segments.name: TVS Credit
segments.commentary: Disbursed to over 14 lakh new customers, taking the customer base to about 2.6 crore. Book size grew 19% and PBT rose 16% to INR 283 crore.

segments.name: Norton
segments.commentary: Manx and Atlas production has started, with Atlas rolling out from Hosur in June. Cumulative investment is about INR 2,000 crore to INR 2,500 crore over the last 4-5 years.

International growth expected at the same rate or slightly better in Q2.

Partnership with IOC for last-mile LPG cylinder distribution and cargo EV mobility.
