qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler capacity is about 40,000 units moving to 50,000+. 3W capacity is moving from about 20,000 to 30,000 units, with EV a good share. EV demand is spreading from urban to semi-urban areas, and some buyers are moving from motorcycles to scooters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is TVS gaining share against a competitor discounting in scooters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a broad scooter range, frequent feature upgrades, durability and JD Power rankings. It said dealer stock is kept below 30 days and that retail financing supports growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the commodity headwind and how much has been passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Most of the impact was in Q1, with some further pressure from aluminium and oil-linked plastics. Price increases were about 1.5% in Q1 and about 0.5% in Q2, with the rest offset by mix, scale and cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Is EV profitability improving?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EV contribution is improving quarter after quarter, but it expects the EV margin to reach the company's target over time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the overall capacity and investment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: 2W capacity is moving from about 6.8 million to 8.3 million units by Q4, with 3W capacity rising to about 0.42 million. Total investment is about INR 3,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Norton strategy, investment and volume ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Four Norton models (Manx, Manx R, Atlas and Atlas GT) are launching across the UK, Europe, India and later the US. The model uses independent dealers and multi-brand premium outlets, with cumulative investment of about INR 2,000-2,500 crore. Management gave no breakeven volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses decline and will that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April production loss and supply issues drove some cost control. It said brand spend as a percentage of sales will not change much, and launch costs will add to expenses when new products are introduced.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 600-700 crore PLI receivable collectible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR 600 crore is PLI receivable and is fully collectible, with the government having always supported the scheme.

532343|2026-09.headline: TVS Motor Q2 FY27 revenue rose 44% to INR17,103 crores and PAT 52% to INR1,377 crores, alongside approval of a consumer finance demerger.
532343|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 delivered record volume (1.9 million units, up 27%), revenue, EBITDA and profit, with EBITDA margin up 30 bps to 13.0%. Management said domestic 2W ICE and EV and 3W all grew faster than industry, and international sales hit a record 5.39 lakh units (up 35%). The Board approved a demerger of the consumer finance and related undertaking (including the TVS Credit Services stake) into a separate listed holding company, with shareholders receiving mirror shareholding; completion is expected around July 2027 appointed date after 8 to 10 months of approvals. Management guided to single-digit industry growth in H2 with base effects, and cost pressure expected to ease in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Domestic 2W
segments.commentary: Total 2W ICE sales grew 20% YoY vs industry 14%; domestic ICE up 16% vs industry 10%. Domestic 2W EV up 129% vs industry 84%. EV penetration of 2W was 11.6% in September (scooters about 22%).

segments.name: Domestic 3W
segments.commentary: ICE plus EV 3W volume about 26,300 units, up 65% from 16,000 vs industry 23%. EV penetration of 3W about 44% in Q2 and about 48% in September.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Record 5.39 lakh units in H1, up 35% YoY; Q2 international 2W ICE up 33% vs industry 27%. International EV sales about 6,930 units in Q2 vs 1,726 last year. Africa was the key driver.

segments.name: TVS Credit (consumer finance)
segments.commentary: Book size INR33,818 crores, up 22% from INR27,807 crores; PBT INR330 crores, up 19% from INR277 crores. Network over 65,000 touch points; 14 lakh new customers in the quarter; customer base about 2.7 crores.

segments.name: Norton (e-bike)
segments.commentary: Manx R and Atlas launches under way in Europe (dealers in UK, Italy, France; Germany and Spain coming); India launch expected in coming months; US preparations underway. Current-quarter e-bike loss is lower than the prior quarter, though brand and launch costs rose.

guidance_outlook: Industry ICE growth in 2W and 3W expected to be single digit in H2 FY27 given the high base from Nov-Dec last year; management said it would wait a couple of weeks for a clearer Q3 view.
TVS expects to outgrow the industry in domestic and international markets in Q3 and Q4.
Material cost increases expected to be unlikely in Q3 and Q4 beyond small increases; Q4 may stabilise or soften.

capex_capacity: EV capacity at about 60,000-65,000 units per month (domestic plus exports), with next-level expansion to about 80,000 planned and under way; Orbiter capacity to be enhanced in Q4.
2W capacity to cross 8 million units; 3W capacity to reach about 0.4 million soon.

qa_highlights.question: How is TVS building EV capacity given supply constraints, and what is the Ronin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: EV industry grew about 75% in H1; capacity now 60,000-65,000 units/month, with 80,000 planned. Ronin is expected to go beyond 15,000 units per month, with new variants and a large capacity investment under way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the structure of the consumer finance demerger and what holdings will TVS Motor keep?
qa_highlights.answer: Demerged undertaking includes the TVS Credit Services investment and some non-core investments, moved to a new company with mirror shareholding. TVS Motor keeps no stake; the TVS Credit business is not being merged into the new entity.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the demerger listing?
qa_highlights.answer: Post shareholder approval and NCLT process, around 8 to 10 months. The appointed date is July 2027, after the NBFC consolidation mandated by RBI (approvals expected by March or April 2027).

qa_highlights.question: What is the valuation and net worth of TVS Credit?
qa_highlights.answer: No valuation is set in a demerger. Net worth is about INR6,500 crores before the proposed INR1,200 crore equity infusion. Management declined to give ROE and ROA figures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for industry growth in H2 and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Single-digit growth expected in Q3 given a high base. Material costs expected to rise less in Q3 and Q4; Q1 to Q2 prices rose 1.6% vs 1.9% material cost increase.

qa_highlights.question: Are EV e-bike losses coming down outside Norton?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-Norton e-mobility losses have been curtailed and will be cut further. The Norton loss is lower than in the prior quarter, but brand and launch costs rose.

risks_watch: Base effect in Nov-Dec: management flagged a high prior-year base, making H2 growth more cautious (single digit expected).
Commodity cost inflation: Q1 to Q2 material costs rose about 1.9%; price actions need to keep pace, and employee and marketing costs rose sharply.
Norton and the e-bike business continue to lose money; cumulative losses about INR1,300 crores over 4-5 years per an analyst; India launch and US plans still pending.
Demerger execution: 8 to 10 months to approvals, NBFC consolidation under RBI direction, and the July 2027 appointed date. Business split and valuation are not yet disclosed.

532356|2026-09.headline: Triveni H1 FY27 PBT swung to ₹131 crore from a ₹25 crore loss, driven by sugar realisations up 9% to ₹4,428/MT.
532356|2026-09.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue rose 5% YoY to ₹3,311 crore and operating margin expanded 383 bps to 6.9%, with PBT of ₹131 crore versus a loss of ₹25 crore. Q2 revenue rose 8% to ₹1,731 crore. Sugar drove the turnaround on higher realisations, lower inventory and lower finance cost, while net debt fell to ₹157 crore from ₹702 crore a year ago. Management flagged a mixed H2: tight domestic sugar stocks support prices, but the ESY 26-27 ethanol tender resets alcohol economics and the Water business needs faster execution.

India has an import allowance of 1 million MT; about 300,000 MT has been imported so far. Management expects a further allowance of at least 2 million MT, mainly raw sugar.

October domestic prices averaged about ₹49/kg before rising sharply in November. Haryana SAP raised by ₹15 to ₹430/quintal for 26-27 and ₹20 to ₹450 for 27-28; UP cane price announcement expected in about three to four weeks.

ESY 26-27 OMC tender: 1,100 crore litres offered, with no offers for juice, syrup or B-heavy molasses ethanol. FCI rice capped at 30% (vs about 40% last year). Maize ethanol price cut by ₹3/litre in the tender.

qa_highlights.question: How much damage has late UP rainfall done to the crop, and how does it compare with Maharashtra and Karnataka?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said damage is hard to quantify and could come as yield loss (lodging) or sucrose loss. Western UP cane is bound, so lodging risk is low. Sampling data shows about 50-70 bps lower recovery YoY for the state, with a clearer read by mid-December to mid-January.

qa_highlights.question: Will the tender-based ethanol economics hold once maize prices stay high?
qa_highlights.answer: Current maize at ₹26-27/kg would fully erode maize-ethanol profitability for standalone plants; integrated multi-feed players are better placed. Triveni procured maize at lower prices earlier, so Q3 is secure, and Q4 depends on the final tender.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for UP cane price and sugar import volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: UP cane price expected around end-November, with no number given. About 300,000 MT of the 1 million MT import allowance has been used, with at least 2 million MT more expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise despite the power transmission demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Suresh Taneja said last year's comparatives show power transmission costs under discontinued operations, so the like-for-like comparison shows no significant increase. Management attributed the rise to the new labour code revising wages for 4,000-plus employees.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company deploy capital given high profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: No meaningful capex is planned. Debt reduction is a priority, but the board wants at least one quarter of cash generation data before deciding on other options.

532365|2026-03.headline: Dynacons FY26 revenue rose about 12% to INR1,424 crore and EBITDA about 41% to INR146 crore, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to about 9% on cost pressure.
532365|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR402 crore (about 22% YoY) and EBITDA of INR36 crore (about 26% YoY). Full-year EBITDA margin rose to 10.2% from 8.1%, and PAT grew about 17% to INR85 crore. Management attributed the Q4 sequential margin dip to AI-driven component cost escalation and supply tightness, which it expects to normalise. Order book was close to INR3,000 crore as of May 30, 2026, and the bidding pipeline was about INR5,100 crore as of May 2026. Analysts pressed on lease-driven depreciation and finance cost, working capital days and unit economics of the as-a-service deals; management declined to disclose IRR, payback, segment order book mix or go-live values.

532388|2026-03.headline: IOB posted FY26 net profit of about Rs 5,208 crore (up 56.16%) and advances growth of 24.16%, with GNPA down to 1.42%.

Guaranteed consideration schedule: ₹121 crore received in October, ₹32 crore in November, ~₹504 crore in February 2027, ₹56 crore in July 2027 and ₹682 crore in December 2028; earn-out (~₹550 crore) based on FY28 EBITDA, not FY27.

Executable orders of about ₹1,000 crore; ~₹379 crore executed to date and ₹600-720 crore expected to execute over the next two quarters, subject to supply chain delays.

Space expected to become revenue-generating in FY28 and EBITDA positive thereafter.

ZEDA pillars: embedded boards with LLM/SLM layers, humanoid/robotics (first order from a US company, Humanoid), data-centre chillers (Google as customer), and semiconductor equipment (Applied Materials as customer).
Supply chain constraints in strategic electronics, PCBs and components (12-18 month lead times) may delay deliveries; some premium cost may be paid, impacting margin by ~2%.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said 72% of consideration is guaranteed (₹1,686 crore of ₹2,275 crore); Q2 decline attributed to salary increments, planned Airbus shutdown and ₹3.7 crore ECL charge; net debt of ~₹525-556 crore mainly from CloudWave acquisition, with ₹85 crore repaid in October.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for ZEDA, including fundraising and acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: ZEDA's four pillars are embedded boards, humanoids, data-centre chillers and semiconductor equipment; acquisitions could more than double its FY26 revenue of ~₹125 crore; a standalone fundraise is under NDA and undisclosed.

risks_watch: Phase two divestment (aerospace engineering services, US$206 million) has slipped from November 2026 to February 2027; closing drives the ~₹1,100 crore Q4 gain and ~₹550 crore earn-out, so timing and new-company regulatory approvals are key to monitor.

Q3 and Q4 FY27 margin path: management targets ~15-16% post-ESOP EBITDA in Q3 and ~20% in Q4 (plus or minus 1%), against 11.4 crore reported EBITDA in Q2; ESOP charge (~₹6 crore a quarter target) and corporate overhead reduction to ~₹12 crore a quarter must materialise.

Renewals are being protected with no losses cited.
Active clients ~213 (down QoQ due to rationalisation, management says now done); top 36 accounts contribute ~80% of business; top 5/10/20/30 accounts grew QoQ.
Unbilled revenue at March 2026 was higher than expected due to delayed client documentation; billing regularised and collections improved in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management on sustaining cc QoQ growth, and what is the vertical demand trend?

qa_highlights.question: Will H1 FY27 deal signings and client count bottom out?

Q2 FY27 margin dilution from wage hike (170-200 bps full impact, ~half in Q2) before productivity offsets.
Manufacturing and E&U (together near 50% of revenue per analyst) remain weak; recovery timing is uncertain.
AI-driven pricing pressure could widen the gap between TCV and revenue.
Unbilled revenue elevated; watch for reduction in subsequent quarters.
No numeric guidance; investors pressed for quantified signings and client metrics and a formal capital allocation policy. Cash of INR2,879 crore unallocated.

532400|2026-09.headline: Birlasoft Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.1% QoQ to $148.3M, EBITDA margin held at 15.2%, but management says order book fell short of expectations.
532400|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 2.1% QoQ in constant currency and dollar terms to $148.3M (INR1,416.2 crore, +2.7% QoQ in rupees). EBITDA was INR215.3 crore (15.2% margin), absorbing about 170 bps of wage-revision impact from July 2026 and investments in sales and service-line capability. Deal signings were $116.1M TCV in Q2 (+9% YoY), with H1 at $285M (+15% YoY), but management said some deals slipped into Q3/Q4 and it was not pleased with order booking. Management said H2 financial performance should beat H1, while declining to give formal guidance.

E&U soft due to ramp-down at one European client

Pricing pressure is seen in competitive deals but not broadly across the mid-market.

qa_highlights.question: Has the exit from low-margin accounts been completed, and is annuity revenue rising?

qa_highlights.question: Was Q2 revenue in line with expectations, and what drove the EBITDA margin walk?

532408|2026-09.headline: Sigma Advanced Systems Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 12% QoQ to INR417 crores, with operational EBITDA of INR82.28 crores (19.7% margin).
532408|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR417 crores in Q2 FY27, up from INR374 crores in Q1, and operational EBITDA rose to INR82.28 crores from INR61 crores at a 19.7% margin. Profit after tax excluding associate share was INR48.6 crores versus INR35.41 crores in Q1. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,900-2,000 crores at about 20% EBITDA margin, and said the UK operations and Sri City facility are moving work to India to lift margins. Management also announced a planned fundraise of up to INR3,000 crores to fund acquisitions, with closings targeted for Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MIL CCF arrangement and time to revenue?

qa_highlights.question: What is the bridge from H1 revenue of about INR800 crores to the INR2,000 crore FY27 target?

qa_highlights.question: How is the debt position and repayment planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is about INR80 crores, mostly working capital; term loan of INR76 crores with repayment strategy not finalised. Other term borrowings follow a schedule running January 1 to December 31, 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the acquisition size and target profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets are businesses with about USD100-150 million revenue, EBITDA positive, with OEM customer access and capacity to transfer work to India. Management said it avoids loss-making companies.

532424|2026-03.headline: GCPL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11% in INR on 6% underlying volume growth; EBITDA up 10% at 21.7% margin, with a revenue-presentation change.
532424|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11% in INR on 6% underlying volume growth, EBITDA grew 10% with a 21.7% margin, and reported PAT grew 10%. India standalone was the standout: 8% volume growth, 10% sales growth, 18% EBITDA growth and a 24.7% margin, led by Home Care (+12%). Africa/US/Middle East grew 20% in sales but EBITDA rose only 2% after doubling media spend, and Indonesia grew 3% in sales with 4% volume growth. From this quarter, customer-related trade spends are netted off revenue following an ICAI Expert Advisory Committee opinion, with no impact on absolute EBITDA or PAT. Management guided to margin pressure in Q1 and likely Q2 FY27 from crude-linked and palm oil input inflation of roughly 7-9%, offset by price hikes and share gains.

financial_highlights.change: Strong in household insecticide, air fresheners, fabric care
Personal Wash gained share; soaps muted
4% underlying volume growth; pricing pressure bottomed out

financial_highlights.metric: Africa, USA and Middle East sales growth
financial_highlights.change: EBITDA +2%, media spend doubled on FMCG categories

financial_highlights.metric: Latin America and others sales growth

guidance_outlook: Q1 and probably Q2 FY27 India EBITDA margins expected below normative levels (about 21.5%), though absolute EBITDA may hold up through higher revenue from pricing.
Raw material inflation cited at 7-9% on a blended basis, based on Brent around USD100-105 and palm oil around MYR4,500.
Price increases taken in April 2026: soaps about 5%, detergents 6-7%, household insecticides 4-5%; management expects to recover most of the cost inflation.
Full-year FY27 volumes may be slightly lower than planned, revenue growth slightly higher, and EBITDA slightly lower than earlier expectations at current costs.

Detailed FY27 guidance and portfolio updates deferred to the analyst investor meet on 11 May 2026.

demand_pricing: India soaps: volumes muted; management attributes this partly to a cooler prior-year summer, a shift to liquid cleansing, and grammage cuts on small packs that are still 15-20% below last year.
Pricing: management said pricing growth is running above its earlier expectation, and soap prices are expected to rise after GST-linked cuts were passed to consumers.
Competition: in detergents GCPL is not the market leader and will follow the leader's pricing; in soaps it is gaining share but category growth is muted.
West Asia conflict is lifting middle-distillate prices (LAB, kerosene), which is a cost headwind for detergents but a competitive positive, since local players are short of feedstock.
Weather: a potential El Nino could weaken Q1 FY27 HI and soap demand, though management expects a better Q2 and Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Personal Care weaker and what is the soaps outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said soap markets are muted after GST and a warm/cold weather swing, that Personal Wash gained share, and that pricing will return to soaps, with Personal Care expected to grow faster in FY27 but structurally slower than Home Care.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 21.5% normative margin for India at risk given inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects lower margins for this quarter and next (about 3-4 months of pressure) because crude costs hit all categories, but it expects EBITDA to recover as pricing and share gains come through.

532424|2026-06.headline: GCPL Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 19% YoY on 9% underlying volume growth, EBITDA up 14% with 19% margin; India gross margin hit by war-linked input costs.
532424|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY with underlying volume growth of 9%, EBITDA rose 14% at a 19% margin, and net profit grew 11%. India gross margin fell sharply as LPG, kerosene and LABSA roughly trebled during the war-driven spike, with India cost impact near 6% over plan. Africa (GAUM) delivered an exceptional quarter with constant-currency growth around 25% and EBITDA margins moving to mid-teens, while Indonesia returned to stable growth at about 10%. Management says it is on track for full-year guidance and expects to exceed it on revenue, and possibly on EBITDA and volume.

segments.name: India Household Insecticides (HI)
segments.commentary: Management says GCPL gained overall HI market share in Q1 FY27 for the first time in almost a decade, driven by incense sticks, not premium segments. June was very weak due to rain and poor fill rates; July first half also poor.

segments.name: India Air care / Speedboats
segments.commentary: Speedboats grew about 3% in Q1 per analyst calculation; salience about 15% and management expects roughly 100-150 bps rise per quarter. Air care in India hit by LPG-linked fill rate falls of 20-25%.

segments.name: Africa / GAUM
segments.commentary: Constant-currency growth about 25%, driven by FMCG (air care at double-digit market share in South Africa within six months of launch) and hair extensions cost improvements. FY26 growth split was about 50:50 FMCG and hair.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Growth about 10% on a slower base, step-up in air media, and early El Nino benefit; Stellar business growing faster.

segments.name: Soaps (India)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew positively in Q1; management expects early single-digit growth in Q2 and Q3, soap margins at normative levels.

segments.name: Muuchstac (acquired DTC brand)
segments.commentary: Growth of about 70-80% from acquisition run rate; EPS accretive from day one, profitable digital-first brand.

segments.name: Pet care
segments.commentary: Committed INR500 crore capital; additional INR200 crore rights commitment referenced by analyst. Product-market fit achieved in Tamil Nadu; expansion to rest of South India under way.

532424|2026-09.headline: GCPL Q2 FY27: consolidated revenue up 19% YoY (15% constant currency) on 8% underlying volume growth; net profit up 14% to INR523 crore.
532424|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY (15% in constant currency) with 8% underlying volume growth, EBITDA grew 12% and net profit rose 14% to INR523 crore. Standalone sales grew 13% on 7% underlying volume growth, after an estimated 150 bps hit from trade inventory correction, which also mildly hit standalone EBITDA. GUAM (Africa) and Indonesia were the strongest international contributors, while input inflation was among the highest in many years and was offset by pricing, cost savings and A&P optimisation. Management held FY27 guidance of high single-digit standalone UVG and double-digit consolidated revenue and EBITDA growth, and said revenues are running ahead of plan.

segments.commentary: Value growth of 8%, with soaps stable despite significant price increases and grammage reduction against a favourable comparator. Premium liquids, Cinthol body wash, hair colour (share gains) and perfumes/deodorants (strong double-digit growth) contributed; volume growth lagged value growth.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Sales +20% with 8% underlying volume growth and EBITDA +12%, aided by El Nino-driven mosquito infestation tailwind; LPG prices doubled. Newer portfolio (LV, Pocket) sustained double-digit underlying volume growth.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline and skill-set for the India CEO hire, and progress on pet care and new bathroom cleaner?
qa_highlights.answer: India CEO search is in a robust process, prioritising Godrej values and entrepreneurial mindset over speed. Godrej Spic is now national. Pet care is still in learning phase; management will give milestones next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Personal Care volume growth well below 8% value growth, and which parts are weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Soaps saw trade inventory correction (large SKUs typically build inventory) and price-volume recalibration after steep price increases; margins still below normative. Hair colour gained share strongly. Detergents growth is in line with trend.

qa_highlights.question: How should Q3/Q4 India margins and EBITDA be viewed given commodity lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity inflation expected slightly higher in Q3 vs Q2. Company will focus on consolidated EBITDA YoY growth rather than margin, aiming to hold double-digit consolidated EBITDA growth; India may see some up-and-down quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are H2 volume risks from inflation or season in detergents and HI?
qa_highlights.answer: Detergents not impacted by inflation on volume; HI season looks fine as El Nino impact was mainly in H1. Management expects to sustain volume trend lines.

qa_highlights.question: Is the decline in India standalone A&P spend structural or cyclical?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: soaps and detergents category spend has fallen and the company is balancing spend to keep share of voice at target, while the rest of the portfolio gets higher reach at lower cost via media agency practices. Management gave roughly equal weight to the two factors.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are Indonesia and GUAM growth beyond this year, and what is GUAM's mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Indonesia: a few bps of this year's growth is attributed to better weather; management is building more growth flywheels and expects double-digit international volume growth. GUAM: growth is broad-based, from core hair and new categories like Mega Growth Mousse and Darling styling products; hair colour has grown double digit in volume for 7-8 quarters. No split of core vs new given.

532432|2026-09.headline: United Spirits Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell 4.3% to Rs 600 crore, with P&A price-mix up 7.4% and marketing spend at 11.6% of net sales.

Management cited West Asia cost inflation of about Rs 50 crore in the quarter, weaker lower-end consumer demand, and a Maharashtra and Karnataka policy drag on the popular segment. The brandy portfolio has been moved into the P&A segment, with prior periods restated. Management reiterated a double-digit P&A growth aspiration for FY27, relying on the Maharashtra lap, the MML brand launches and innovation in H2, and kept the DJ-related deal on track for a mid-December longstop date.

532440|2026-09.headline: MPS raised FY27 EBITDA floor to at least INR 310 crore; H1 revenue up 17.8% to INR 448.5 crore at a 34.3% EBITDA margin.
532440|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 was described as the most profitable half in MPS history, with revenue up 17.8% to INR 448.5 crore and EBITDA up 39% to INR 154 crore at a 34.3% margin. Q2 revenue was roughly flat sequentially, which management attributed to timing: large research mandates only begin billing in November and December, and Education and Corporate Learning follow adoption calendars. Management raised its FY27 EBITDA floor from above INR 300 crore to at least INR 310 crore, and reiterated the INR 1,500 crore FY28 revenue ambition, which now depends on an acquisition expected to close this financial year. The company carries zero debt and INR 163 crore of cash.

segments.commentary: Now 30.6% of group revenue; H1 revenue +36%, EBITDA +14.5%. Bookings led by Florida's upcoming math adoption, with California to follow. Unbound contributed INR 41.6 crore in H1 and its margin rose from 12-13% at acquisition to about 18%.

segments.name: Corporate Learning
segments.commentary: H1 margin rose to 25% from about 16%, with EBITDA up 77% and 19% fewer people. Q2 revenue grew 17%. A four-year program with a large US university was won, combining Unbound and Liberate.

capex_capacity: Hiring ahead of the new research mandates to ensure reliable delivery; headcount rising, while EBITDA per employee rose about 15% in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: With no acquisition announced since Unbound, how is progress toward the INR 1,500 crore FY28 target, and where is the next deal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target combines organic growth and acquisitions and expects the next acquisition to close this financial year. It has walked away from deals priced above what it considers their worth, and has zero debt and INR 163 crore cash.

qa_highlights.question: What are the non-Unbound niche criteria for future acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Assets must have AI tailwinds, operate in science or high-stakes content, have low customer concentration, a recurring revenue theme, a defensible niche, and a clear way to plug into MPS.

qa_highlights.question: Why was sequential revenue almost flat in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to timing: new research mandates bill from November and December, and Education and Corporate Learning follow adoption and project timing. Growth is expected to build in H2, with Q4 weighted.

qa_highlights.question: How could a Democratic Congress affect MPS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects it to make deep NIH and NSF cuts less likely and to protect federal nursing workforce programs, which the administration had proposed cutting about 70%. It sees this as a positive for research, healthcare, and education demand.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI causing pricing pressure in research, and are clients reluctant to sign longer contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts remain three to five years and pricing is a win-win in which lower rates are offset by volume. Throughput, not price, is the main client consideration.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Unbound margin lever progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Unbound margin rose from 12-13% at acquisition to about 18%. The next step toward the 20s is expected to come from revenue growth rather than cost cuts.

qa_highlights.question: Why is AJE still struggling to grow, and what is its payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AJE is strategically important as the AI language engine and an entry point to research integrity work. Payback on the roughly INR 70 crore purchase is estimated at 2 to 2.5 years, and ROCE is about 35%.

532443|2026-03.headline: Cera Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.4% YoY to INR 644 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.2% from 18.3% on brass costs and trade discounts.
532443|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11.4% YoY to INR 644 crore, led by volume (about 12%), with management citing early retail recovery from Q3 and continued project strength. EBITDA excluding other income fell to INR 98 crore (15.2% margin) from INR 106 crore (18.3%), driven by brass input costs, elevated trade discounts and pre-operating costs for Senator and Polipluz. Price increases were taken in March (11% effective) and April-May (surcharge then 8% sanitaryware and 5% faucetware), with management targeting a 14-15% EBITDA margin. Morbi gas disruptions were cited as an opportunity, with Cera running inventory and internalising outsourced SKUs. FY26 revenue was INR 2,050 crore, and FY27 guidance is 18-20% growth.

demand_pricing: Management says retail demand improved from Q3 FY26, continued through Q4 and into April 2026; project share has risen from about 30% to 39-40% and is expected to stabilise, with a 60:40 retail-to-project split.

Management says the two-month effective increase is 12% for sanitaryware and 16% for faucetware, applied to retail; projects keep old prices for up to one year from booking.

Brass prices up about 29-30% YoY, moving from late INR 600s to INR 800-850 per kg range (as stated). Management says the 16% faucetware price increase covers about 18% COGS impact, leaving a 1-2% gap to be recovered through discount control.
Q4 volume-led growth: volume about 12%, product mix 3-4%, price/discount drag about 3%. Product mix: premium 41%, mid 38%, entry 21%. Tier-3 40%, Tier-1 36%, Tier-2 24%.
Peers' price increases reportedly 16-18% for faucets and 10-12% for sanitaryware; management says Cera is in line.
FY27 volume guidance: sanitaryware 7-8%, faucetware 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: How is retail demand likely to evolve in FY27, and what is the institution-versus-retail balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail recovered from Q3 and continued into April, and project share rose from about 30% to 39-40%. It expects a stable 60:40 retail-to-project mix and FY27 volume growth of 7-8% for sanitaryware and 10-12% for faucetware.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the price increase delayed, and how much more is needed to protect the margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Brass rose from late INR 600s to INR 800-850 per kg with about 29-30% YoY. Cera has taken about 12% on sanitaryware and 16% on faucetware over two months, with project pricing lagging by about six months. The remaining 1-2% gap is expected to be recovered through discounts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Senator and Polipluz revenue, target and breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue was about INR 19 crore (Senator 10.5, Polipluz 8.5), with a FY27 target of INR 70-80 crore. Management said the brands make a small profit before publicity and expect to be profitable after publicity next year.

qa_highlights.question: How does 18-20% overall growth reconcile with 12% sanitaryware and 18% faucetware growth?
qa_highlights.answer: The balance comes from tiles and construction chemicals (about INR 250 crore, 20%-plus growth once Morbi normalises) and Senator/Polipluz (INR 70-80 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Why are trade discounts still high when retail demand is recovering, and what is the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said discounts rose through the downturn and cannot be cut immediately; control starts from Q1 FY27. Q4 margin rose to 15.2% from 10.2% in Q3, and management expects 14-15% to be sustained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sanitaryware capacity utilisation, inventory and supply outlook for Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanitaryware utilisation was 70% in March; one kiln was closed. Management said inventory covers about 2-3 months of forecast demand, and tiles are expected to be impacted in Q1 because they are fully outsourced.

qa_highlights.question: What are the employee cost trends and capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 included about INR 5 crore of wage code provision, and Q4 had a INR 10 crore exceptional write-back on gratuity and PL liability. Employee cost is expected to rise about 10% in FY27. Capex is guided at about INR 43-45 crore including office space of about INR 15 crore.

risks_watch: Morbi gas-driven supply disruption: sanitaryware outsourcing is about 60% (mostly Morbi) and tiles are almost fully outsourced; management expects Q1 FY27 tiles to be impacted and Morbi sanitaryware output to stay slow through monsoon, with internalised SKUs only available from Q2 FY27.

Price-cost gap: management says the 16% faucetware and 12% sanitaryware price increases cover brass costs only partly (about 1-2% gap on faucetware), and project pricing lags by about six months since projects keep old prices for up to a year from booking.
Trade discounts: margin recovery to 14-15% depends on discount control starting Q1 FY27; Q4 margin was 15.2% versus 10.2% in Q3, and Q4 benefited from inventory liquidation during Morbi disruption.

FY27 growth bridge: 18-20% overall growth relies on tiles and construction chemicals (about INR 250 crore, 20%-plus growth) and Senator/Polipluz (INR 70-80 crore) versus FY26 Senator/Polipluz revenue of about INR 19 crore and losses of about INR 8.5 crore; sustained losses and publicity spend (INR 10-12 crore) are a watch item.

Cost and capex items to track: pending labour long-term settlement could add wage cost on top of about 10% employee cost rise; greenfield sanitaryware first phase now about INR 150 crore with construction timing undecided; sanitaryware utilisation at 70-75% and second kiln restart timing.
key_quotes: Since Q3 of the current financial year, we have started seeing an improvement in the retail demand, and we saw this sustaining through Q4 also.
So, these trade discounts are again can be corrected it in the coming quarters.
Tiles will be impacted, because in the month of March, also later part of March, most of it is dependent upon outsourcing.
So, we anticipate that the current situation would be playing well for us going forward in Q1 and Q2.

rows.why: Order book of 18 crore litres is 5 crore litres below the 23 crore applied for, and only about 50% was fulfilled by March, so the June tenders must close the gap or volumes fall short of plan.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Specialty and import-substitute chemicals are part of the INR 500 crore Narsinghpur project, but it only starts in FY28 and no specific product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Ethanol order book top-up to 22 crore litres
rows.why: Order book fell to 18 crore litres from 21 crore litres last year, against 23 crore applied for; management expects at least 22 crore litres within FY27 and about 9 crore litres still to be fulfilled over the remaining two quarters.

rows.label: Maize cost relief in H2 FY27
rows.why: MP maize may fall to INR 18-19/kg from INR 22 and Assam/Muzaffarnagar around INR 22, versus ethanol EBITDA break-even at about INR 24/kg, so the cost tailwind is conditional on prices holding.

rows.label: Debt-free by FY29 ex-Assam term loan
rows.why: Total debt is about INR 313 crore today, and management says the company could be debt-free by FY29 except the Assam loan running to FY32, though the INR 500 crore capex funding is undecided.

tone.note: Management was confident on ethanol demand, E30 readiness and FY27 margin sustainability, but evasive on the order-book shortfall (18 vs 23 crore litres applied for) and on capex funding and timing; analysts pressed on those gaps.

532457|2026-06.headline: Gulshan Polyols Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR646 crore (+8% YoY) and EBITDA rose 135% to INR91 crore, a 14.2% margin.
532457|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of about INR646 crore was the highest quarterly turnover in company history, up 8% YoY. EBITDA of INR91 crore grew 135% YoY, with margin at 14.2% versus 6.5% a year earlier, and PAT of INR54 crore rose about 307% YoY. Ethanol was the main driver with an 18% segment EBITDA margin, while grain processing improved from weak levels and mineral chemicals stayed steady. Management called Q1 exceptional on favourable raw material prices and high DDGS prices, and kept FY27 guidance unchanged while signalling a conservative stance.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue INR426 crore and EBITDA INR81 crore (18% margin); largest contributor to revenue and profit. Installed capacity about 26 crore litres per annum; order book about 19 crore litres.

segments.name: Grain processing (starch, sorbitol, derivatives)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR170 crore and EBITDA INR8 crore in Q1. FY27 guidance is revenue about INR800 crore at about 5% EBITDA margin; no capacity expansion this year.

segments.name: Mineral chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR24 crore and EBITDA INR5 crore (23% margin). Described as stable; no significant capacity expansion planned.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of about INR2,600 crore, unchanged.
Ethanol revenue about INR1,700-1,800 crore on supplies of about 22 crore litres (Q&A cited 21-22 crore litres generating about INR1,800 crore).
Grain processing revenue about INR800 crore; mineral processing about INR100 crore.
Consolidated EBITDA margin about 10-11% and PAT margin about 5-6%; management said it expects to end the year above these margins but is guiding conservatively.
Ethanol debottlenecking to lift utilisation to 100-110% of existing capacity by FY28, with capacity up about 15-20%.
On-site plant at Trident expected to be operational by end of FY27, adding some revenue.
capex_capacity: Majority of recent capex is complete; FY27 focus is on utilisation and cash flow, with only ethanol debottlenecking planned.
Major expansion into specialty and import-substitute chemicals, grain-based derivatives, expected from FY28; products still under evaluation and not yet named.
Starch capacity to be ramped to 100% utilisation by end of FY27; no starch expansion this year.
Capital subsidy of INR5 crore received from Madhya Pradesh in Q2, adjusted against plant and machinery capex.
Ethanol plants at Assam and Madhya Pradesh; four plants in total grinding about 3,000 tonnes of grain per day.
demand_pricing: Government support for ethanol: E20 achieved; E30 targeted by 2030. Management said higher blending beyond 20% may slip 6-12 months because of protests, but E20 will not be rolled back.
Ethanol feedstock mix: about 40% FCI rice, about 50% maize, about 10% broken rice/DDGS.

Maize prices currently INR23-25/kg across plants (Assam 23, Muzaffarnagar 23, Gujarat 24, MP 25); Q1 raw-material costs were favourable and Q2 is seasonally pressured until the Kharif harvest in October-November.
Maize DDGS priced at about INR20-22; stable for about two quarters. DDGS contributes about INR10 per litre of ethanol cost.
Grain processing: domestic starch and derivative prices improved as exports began from Gujarat; sorbitol exported to more than 40 countries. Management expects a sharp YoY improvement in the segment.
Inventory cap of 30-45 days of grain because of storage and working-capital limits, so raw-material volatility is only partly hedged.
Talks on opening ethanol exports to neighbouring countries (Japan, Indonesia mentioned in press); not yet started.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong Q1 ethanol margin a one-off, given FY guidance of about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was exceptional on favourable raw material prices and record DDGS prices. Q2 is seasonally weak, and H2 (Q3-Q4) is usually stronger; guidance is conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Will E30 timelines slip given protests?
qa_highlights.answer: E20 will not be rolled back. E30 is set for 2030, and blending beyond 20% may be delayed by 6-12 months. Steady-state ethanol demand is not expected to be affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ethanol order book and how confident is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: About 19 crore litres already received, with about 2 crore litres more expected. Management is confident of 21-22 crore litres for FY27, generating about INR1,800 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw-material price volatility managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Stocking is capped at 30-45 days of grain. Management will stock up during the April and October harvests, and the full-year margin is expected to average out.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term ethanol growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity to rise 15-20% through debottlenecking, targeting 100-110% utilisation of existing capacity by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the grain processing underperformance and what is the recovery outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recovery has started with a big YoY margin improvement. Starch capacity is to reach 100% by year-end, with FY27 grain processing EBITDA margin about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export exposure and hedging approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about INR18 crore, or 5-6% of quarterly turnover. The company does not hedge FX and relies on a natural hedge from equivalent imports.

qa_highlights.question: Were any government subsidies recognised in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Grants and incentives are accounted for on a receipt basis, and nothing was received in Q1. INR5 crore MP capital subsidy was received in Q2 and adjusted against capex.

risks_watch: Q2 seasonal pressure on maize and grain costs before the Kharif harvest; margins may fall short of Q1 levels.
Possible 6-12 month delay to blending beyond E20 because of protests, which could slow incremental ethanol allocations.
Grain processing (starch) remains low-margin, around 5% EBITDA guided, with a recovery still to be proven.
Specialty chemical expansion from FY28 has no named products or capex figure yet.
Ethanol export opening is still at talk stage; timing is uncertain.
Reliance on OMC purchase orders for the 2 crore litre balance not yet received.
key_quotes: So, we are just talking on more conservative guidance we have given for the year, and I hope that we are doing better, we ultimately perform better than what we are guiding.
The increasing blending beyond 20% may be delayed by 6 months to 1 year until these unnecessary social media noise settles down.
R&D process is going on, but we will not be able to give out any name until it has been finalized by the board.
There has been protest, but that is really temporary. The government will not roll back for sure.

rows.why: FY27 guidance was held at INR2,600 crore revenue and 10-11% EBITDA despite Q1 margin of 14.2%, and management said it expects to end above these margins, but this is conditional on H2 seasonal strength.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 raw-material pressure before the Kharif harvest in October-November could pull margins below Q1 levels, and E20-plus blending may slip 6-12 months, though guidance is held.

rows.why: The specialty chemical products are not yet named and are still under evaluation, with no product launch timeline beyond FY28 start.

rows.label: Ethanol raw-material cost and DDGS tailwind fading in Q2
rows.why: Q1 raw-material costs were favourable and DDGS priced INR20-22 (stable about two quarters), but Q2 is seasonally pressured until the Kharif harvest in October-November, with maize at INR23-25/kg.

rows.label: Ethanol order book and OMC purchase orders
rows.why: About 19 crore litres already received with about 2 crore litres more expected, but the 2 crore litre balance still depends on OMC purchase orders not yet received, against a 21-22 crore litre FY27 target.

rows.label: Ethanol exports to neighbouring countries
rows.why: Talks on Japan and Indonesia are reported in press but not yet started, so timing is uncertain and no volume is guided.

532457|2026-09.headline: Gulshan Polyols H1 FY27 PAT rose 222% to INR92 crore and EBITDA margin hit 12.7%, but management flags Q3–Q4 margin pressure from record maize prices.
532457|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was INR614 crore (+13% YoY), EBITDA INR69 crore (+63%) at 11.2% margin, and PAT INR39 crore (+151%), driven by ethanol profitability. H1 FY27 EBITDA reached INR159 crore (+97%) at 12.7% margin, with PAT of INR92 crore. Management said record maize prices (INR30–32/kg) will pressure margins in Q3 and possibly Q4, but kept FY27 guidance unchanged. Debt fell to about INR233 crore from INR312 crore at FY26 end, and the company announced sorbitol and MDP/NDC expansions at Muzaffarnagar plus a green hydrogen BOO arrangement.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR427 crore with EBITDA INR62.5 crore (14.6% margin, vs 8.5% a year earlier). Company secured an allocation of 19.7 crore litres, with an order book of about INR1,300 crore plus about INR300 crore from by-products (about INR1,600 crore total).

segments.name: Grain processing
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR166 crore (+24% YoY) but EBITDA only INR2.45 crore (1.5% margin). Management attributes losses to the starch plant, which does not cover variable cost due to starch overcapacity in India.

segments.name: Mineral chemicals
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR22.7 crore and EBITDA INR4.6 crore (20.2% margin). On-site PCC slurry plant at Trident's Barnala site (22,000 tpa) is due April 2027, expected to add about INR20 crore revenue a year from FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: consolidated revenue about INR2,600 crore (ethanol INR1,700–1,800 crore, grain processing about INR800 crore, mineral about INR100 crore).
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin target of 10% and PAT margin about 5%.
Management said Q3 and possibly Q4 margins will be affected; ethanol margin guided at 11–12% for the full year. Consolidated EBITDA expected around 9–11%, and better than 10% as in FY26.
FY28 consolidated revenue target INR2,800–3,000 crore; management called the INR3,000 crore milestone achievable subject to execution and markets.
Ethanol volume: expects to execute about 22 crore litres by end of ESY 2026-27, with debottlenecking aimed at 24–25 crore litres.
capex_capacity: Sorbitol: new 30,000 tpa plant at Muzaffarnagar (UP), taking total sorbitol capacity to 1,10,000 tpa; aimed at North and Northeast India markets. Existing sorbitol capacity is in Gujarat (Bharuch).
MDP/NDC: expansion from 5,000 tpa to 30,000 tpa at Muzaffarnagar, flexible between maltodextrin powder and non-dairy creamer. Indicative mix about 20,000 t MDP and 10,000 t NDC.

Combined project cost about INR120 crore, funded about INR100 crore bank debt and about INR20 crore internal accruals. Commissioning targeted May 2027. Expected revenue INR200–250 crore at optimal levels (about 10–11% EBITDA margin); initial year INR120–130 crore; 2–3 year ramp-up.

Green hydrogen: ZFI to build, own and operate a 6 MW green hydrogen plant at the sorbitol facility under BOO model, with INR300 crore long-term contract over 10 years. Management expects about 20% cost saving versus open-market hydrogen and about 15,000 t annual CO2 reduction.
CWIP of about INR15 crore spread across Muzaffarnagar, Bharuch and Borgaon for ongoing capex. Management said the major ethanol investment phase is largely complete.
demand_pricing: Maize procurement prices are at record levels of INR30–32/kg, up from INR20–21/kg earlier. Management expects elevated prices for the next 2–3 months due to El Niño.
Ethanol becomes unviable above maize at INR26–27/kg; positive EBITDA is sustainable up to INR26/kg.

Feedstock allocation from OMCs: about 25% FCI rice, about 10% damaged food grains (DFG), and balance maize. Switching from maize to DFG/FCI rice takes 2–3 hours. OMCs save INR4–5 per litre on switching, and DDGS prices have provided a cushion.
Inventory rose about INR60 crore in the quarter as the company bought grain ahead of expected price moves and future grinding needs.
Country liquor (ENA) order of about INR100 crore for FY27 is tender-based and available once a year, with better margins than fuel ethanol. Selling prices: NDC about INR150/kg, MDP about INR50/kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current feedstock mix and how much of the shift to FCI rice and damaged grains is done?
qa_highlights.answer: Current allocation is about 25% FCI rice, 10% DFG and the balance maize. Management can request switches from maize to DFG when maize is not viable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the open market maize price, and will it moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize is INR30–32/kg, an all-time high. Industry is lobbying for an import duty cut. Management expects prices to stay elevated for the next 2–3 months.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about Q3 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margin pressure in Q3. H1 results give a cushion to meet full-year guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Muzaffarnagar expansion lift grain processing profitability, and how is it funded?
qa_highlights.answer: The expansion moves output away from starch, which is loss-making, toward sorbitol, MDP and NDC. Expected revenue is INR200–250 crore at about 10–11% EBITDA margin, funded about INR100 crore debt and INR20 crore internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA per litre by feedstock, and can feedstock switches happen without restriction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-feedstock EBITDA changes daily and declined to give it, but reiterated 11–12% ethanol margin guidance. There are no technical bottlenecks to switching feedstock.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise about INR60 crore, and will it normalise in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was built in advance of expected scarcity and rising prices to protect margins and cover future grinding. Management did not give a normalisation timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the subsidy and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: A INR5 crore capital subsidy from Assam under NEIDS was netted against capex, not in P&L. Long-term debt is about INR123 crore (SBI INR103 crore, HSBC INR22 crore), with HSBC repaid by February 2027. A INR100 crore project loan sanction is expected in 2–3 quarters.

risks_watch: Maize at INR26–27/kg is the viability threshold for ethanol; Q3 and Q4 margins are expected to be pressured, and Q3 comparisons will be against a stronger base.
Working capital: the INR60 crore inventory build and any reversal could affect cash flow and debt.
Execution risk on the May 2027 Muzaffarnagar commissioning and the ramp-up over 2–3 years, plus the April 2027 Barnala PCC plant.
Green hydrogen plant (ZFI BOO, INR300 crore over 10 years) is a first-of-kind on-site set-up for the company and depends on the operator's delivery.
Policy: import duty on maize and OMC allocation rules; ethanol debottlenecking from 22 to 24–25 crore litres is not yet confirmed.

So, we are hoping to keep it around 9% to 11% maximum, not beyond that.
Maize prices are at an all-time high. The country has never seen these kinds of maize prices which they are seeing today.

rows.why: Debt fell to about INR233 crore from INR312 crore at FY26 end and HSBC INR22 crore loan is due for repayment by February 2027, though a INR100 crore project loan sanction is expected in 2-3 quarters that would add back debt.

532461|2026-03.headline: PNB Q4 FY26 net profit rose 14.4% YoY to INR5,225 crore; GNPA fell to 2.95% and FY27 NIM guided at 2.6-2.7%.
532461|2026-03.overview: Punjab National Bank reported Q4 FY26 net profit of INR5,225 crore (up 14.4% YoY) and operating profit of INR7,500 crore (up 10.7% YoY), with FY26 operating profit growth of 9.2% above its 8-9% guidance. Asset quality improved: GNPA fell to 2.95% from 3.95% and NNPA to 0.29% from 0.40%, with FY26 slippage ratio at 0.60%. Domestic NIM was 2.61% in Q4 and global NIM 2.47%, below earlier guidance of 2.8-2.9%, and management cut FY27 global NIM guidance to 2.6-2.7%. Management said the Q4 employee cost fall reflected a INR2,121 crore positive impact from AS-15 yield hardening, which flatters profit, and it framed the ECL transition from April 2027 as manageable.

financial_highlights.change: +10.7% YoY vs INR6,776 crore; FY26 +9.2% vs 8-9% guidance
stable across all four quarters of FY26

segments.name: Retail (ex-IBPC)
segments.commentary: Retail book excluding IBPC grew 18.2% YoY; total retail outstanding about INR2.80 lakh crore including IBPC of INR34,049 crore, which management plans to cut by a further INR18,000-20,000 crore.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 19.9% YoY and management cited ~20% QoQ growth; Q4 MSME slippage INR1,106 crore vs INR995 crore a year earlier. Standard MSME advance yield is 9%.

segments.name: Agriculture (priority sector)
segments.commentary: Agri priority sector advances grew 16.2% YoY; Q4 agri slippage INR1,069 crore vs INR1,400 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate share of loan book is about 46-47%, targeted to fall to 42% short term and 40% long term; corporate standard yield is 7.55%. Sanctioned over INR4 lakh crore of corporate credit lines in FY26, with INR1.18 lakh crore pending disbursement.

guidance_outlook: Global NIM guided at 2.6-2.7% for FY27, versus 2.8-2.9% earlier; management will revisit the guidance in October after Q1 and Q2 review.
NII growth guided at about 7% for FY27 alongside 12-13% credit growth; management called it conservative and said it may revisit in October.
Management expects Q1 and Q2 FY27 NIM to improve QoQ, with cost of deposits falling about 5 bps from the special-scheme repricing and incremental deposit cost falling 2-3 bps a month.

ECL transition from 1 April 2027: management said capital (CRAR 17.74%), the INR2,045 crore floating provision and 97% PCR are sufficient; final ECL impact to be quantified in about two quarters (by July).
Plans to open 250 branches in FY27 (primarily South and West) after adding 144 in FY26; LCR to be maintained around 125%.
Credit cost guidance for FY27 is below 0.4%, as referenced by an analyst; no change was disputed on the call.
capex_capacity: Added 144 branches in FY26 and plans 250 more in FY27, mainly in Southern and Western regions.
New zonal office in Bengaluru operationalised.

No fresh capital raise planned: FY26 had INR8,000 crore authorisation (INR4,000 crore CET1 and INR4,000 crore AT1) but no issuance; INR5,890 crore of AT1 and Tier 2 bonds mature in the current year and will not be replaced.
Wage revision due 1 November 2027, so no FY27 provision was taken for it.
demand_pricing: Total SMA-0/1/2 book is INR41,534 crore (3.30% of advances): SMA-0 INR24,643 crore, SMA-1 INR13,970 crore, SMA-2 INR2,922 crore; retail 8.21%, agri 3.06%, MSME 6.43%.
Q4 FY26 fresh slippages INR2,674 crore vs INR2,904 crore a year earlier; FY26 slippages INR2,758 crore vs INR3,001 crore in FY25. Recoveries of INR15,501 crore in FY26 (2.4x slippages).
Digital sanctions exceeded INR1 lakh crore on a gross basis; INR20,873 crore disbursed digitally in Q4 to 4.8 lakh customers, about one in three loans.
Deposit rates remained sticky; management said cost of deposits has not fallen as expected despite the repo cut, and the Dec-2025 cut hit fully in Q4 versus 26 days in Q3.
Yield on standard domestic advances is 8.23%, above the 7.55% corporate yield.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall sharply QoQ to INR3,747 crore and what is the AS-15 effect?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Raman Grover said AS-15 provisions of INR1,150 crore, INR700 crore and INR700 crore were booked in Q1-Q3; in Q4 no further provision was needed due to bond yield hardening, so INR736 crore is held as prepaid AS-15 and INR1,814 crore was booked to employee cost. Total positive impact cited as INR2,121 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the tax rate rise to about 26.16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 tax was booked at the 25.168% rate plus disallowances, giving an effective 26.16%; Q3 had a reversal of about INR506 crore of earlier provisions, which lowered the Q3 rate to 19.44%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was NIM guided down to 2.6-2.7% and can it return to 2.8-2.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Chandra said deposit rates stayed elevated and bond yields are high, so management chose a conservative 2.6-2.7% range, to be reviewed in Q3 FY27 after watching Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How do 12-13% credit growth and 7% NII growth reconcile with NIM expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NII guidance is conservative given the uncertain corporate book; RAM share is ~54% and targeted to reach 56-57% this year, with corporate falling toward 40% long term, which should lift yields.

qa_highlights.question: Was the ILFS and Sterling Biotech write-back accounted for, and why did standard asset provisions reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Sterling Biotech (a technical write-off) was factored into operating profit. ILFS is still held under standard provision and may be released in Q1 or Q2. The INR727 crore standard-asset provision release reflects RBI's modified large borrower framework effective 1 January 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition impact and effect on run-rate credit cost and ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the final number awaits about two more quarters; the earlier draft estimate was INR9,000-10,000 crore shortfall. Management said the INR2,045 crore floating provision and 97% PCR can absorb it and that ROA will stay above 1%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on the West Asia conflict's impact on MSME and exporters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has seen no challenge in the book so far and held two webinars with exporters and importers in affected areas.

risks_watch: ECL transition from April 2027: final impact unquantified, with management reviewing in about two quarters (by July) and the INR9,000-10,000 crore draft shortfall figure not confirmed.
NIM and cost of deposits: Q4 NIM 2.61% domestic and 2.47% global; cost of deposits fell only 4 bps in Q4 and management expects only about 5 bps further improvement.

The bank set aside an additional INR 700 crore general/standard provision, stated as not affecting net profit or capital, and Q4 profit was supported by a INR 1,567 crore write-off recovery (including a INR 658 crore Sterling Biotech settlement) and a lower employee cost due to a discount-rate change. 532483|2026-09.headline: Canara Bank Q2 FY27: record quarterly net profit of ₹5,175 crore (+8.40% YoY) with Gross NPA down to 1.33%, while ECL transition provisioning now seen at ₹12,000–15,000 crore.
532483|2026-09.overview: Management reported total business crossing ₹30 lakh crore (+15.88% YoY), advances +19.46% and deposits +13.13%, with NII up 20.39% and NIM at 2.53% annual / 2.55% quarterly. Asset quality improved further: Gross NPA 1.33%, Net NPA 0.30%, PCR 95.34% (+175 bps YoY), annualised slippage 0.58% and credit cost 0.47%. Treasury turned into a loss versus the prior year, with MTM about ₹600 crore lower QoQ for the quarter, and management flagged the RBI ECL transition as a ₹12,000–15,000 crore one-time provision requirement. CASA at 29% was the only guidance miss, which management attributed to ₹55,000 crore of FCNR(B) deposits.

financial_highlights.change: FY27 guidance was 1.50% GNPA and ~0.40% NNPA
Agri ₹687 cr, MSME ₹777 cr, Retail ₹327 cr, Corporate ₹13 cr, Gold ₹40 cr

segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 21.03% YoY; MSME +15.49% YoY; Retail slippages ₹327 crore and MSME slippages ₹777 crore in Q2.

segments.commentary: Total agri ₹3.04 lakh crore: gold agri ₹1.74 lakh crore (~₹1.51 lakh crore QoQ) and core agri ₹1.30 lakh crore (~₹1.25 lakh crore QoQ), core agri growing about 9%. Agri slippages ₹687 crore.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Total gold loans ₹2.82 lakh crore (agri ₹1.74 lakh crore, non-agri ₹1.08 lakh crore). Incremental gold yield rose to 9.10% from 8.96% QoQ; gold slippages ₹40 crore.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Incremental corporate yield 7.72% vs 7.68% in Q1; ~₹47,000–50,000 crore of sanctioned-not-disbursed plus hot leads (₹30,000 crore hot leads, ₹17,000 crore sanctioned) in power, green energy, BESS, data centres and HAM roads.

segments.name: Treasury / investments
segments.commentary: Investment book 80% HTM and ~20% AFS/FVTPL; AFS losses ~₹1,300 crore for the quarter go to AFS reserve, not P&L; FVTPL <4% of book. Yields hardened 44 bps in the quarter, ~₹600 crore MTM hit (QoQ basis).

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Canbank Factors stake sale done: ₹14 crore investment, expected ~4x return. Canara HSBC Life and Canara Robeco AMC are listed in the plan.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance (set at start of year): total business +10–11% (delivered +15.88%), advances +11–12% (delivered +19.46%), deposits +9–10% (delivered +13.13%), CASA 30–32% (delivered 29%), NIM 2.50–2.60%, ROE 16.5%, EPS ₹20, ROA 1.01–1.05%; management said it does not plan to revise guidance and will try to better it.

NIM expected to sustain around 2.55% and the 25 bps repo hike is in the book; 53% of the book is repo-linked and already repriced. FCNR(B) leverage spread of only 40–50 bps is expected to be compensated from Q3.

ECL transition one-time provision now estimated at ₹12,000–15,000 crore (up from ₹10,000–12,000 crore), including HTM; management sees up to ₹14,000–15,000 crore if yields stay hardened, with possible return to ₹10,000–12,000 crore if oil prices and geopolitics ease. Impact about 1–1.2% of CRAR/CET1 basis; spread over 1–2 years (5-year option allowed, but not expected).

Management does not expect the ECL provision to materially hit ROA; it said ROA could settle near 0.80% if provisions are not passed on, but would be above 1% if passed through. No decision yet on passing through.
Management expects to complete ECL model dry run within the current quarter (before 31 March 2027 deadline).
capex_capacity: Capex/capacity disclosure is absent: no capex plan, branch or technology spend figures were given; management said it is investing heavily in digital advancements (QR, school fee modules, internet payment gateways) without quantification.
Balance sheet capacity: CRAR 17.19% and CET1 12.80% vs regulatory minimums of 11.5% and 8.5%; management said RWA density is falling quarter-on-quarter.
ECL model build: dry run with technology partner Coforge expected within the current quarter, ahead of the 31 March 2027 deadline.
Liquidity: LCR 115% as of 30 September 2026; FCNR(B) raised $5.8 billion (~₹55,000 crore), of which $3.2 billion funded advances and the rest replaced bulk deposits.

demand_pricing: Retail demand robust with festive season; housing growth 17–18% and total retail ~21%; vehicle loans +25%; management says festive mode already started before Dussehra.
Gold loans: competition rising from large NBFCs; management says Canara prices below NBFCs (which borrow from banks) and sees gold yields rising further as rates harden.

Deposit cost: bulk deposits held at ~₹4.38 lakh crore (vs ₹4.37 lakh crore in Q1). FCNR(B) raised $5.8 billion (~₹55,000 crore), of which $3.2 billion funded advances and the rest replaced bulk deposits; overall cost of deposits lower by ~1%.
Drought: 3 states declared drought-affected (part of Karnataka and Maharashtra cited); exposure ~₹13,900 crore; restructuring to be handled via SLBC dispensation.
Digital fee income: UPI MDR not yet quantified; ai1Pe PSP platform has limited traction; management sees little fee upside currently.

qa_highlights.question: What are incremental yields on corporate and gold loans, and will NIM improve from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate incremental yield 7.72% (vs 7.68% Q1); gold 9.10% (vs 8.96%). Management expects NIM to hold around 2.55% with 53% of the book already repriced and MCLR resets to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Why is bulk deposit flat if FCNR(B) was raised; what is the NIM offset?
qa_highlights.answer: FCNR(B) fully replaced bulk deposits and saved ~100 bps on the replaced portion (6.5% vs 7.5%) plus CRR/SLR cost benefits. Bulk held at ₹4.38 lakh crore; the FCNR leverage spread (40–50 bps) should be offset from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL one-time provision and how will it hit net worth and ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Estimate ₹12,000–15,000 crore including HTM (RBI allows 5 years). Management prefers to spread over 1–2 years; expects PCR to rise to 96–97% and profit >₹20,000 crore to absorb it without denting ROA.

qa_highlights.question: Will the drought affect recoveries and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Drought exposure is ~₹13,900 crore; SLBC restructuring/moratorium expected. Total stress including SMA-0 is 2.42% (₹33,340 crore); >₹5 crore tickets stress 0.30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the treasury/MTM impact and AFS reserve position?
qa_highlights.answer: AFS losses ~₹1,300 crore go to reserve; FVTPL loss ~₹600 crore QoQ swing (Q1 +₹555 crore, Q2 -₹55 crore). Yields hardened 44 bps in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Canbank Factors sale and recovery trend on written-off accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Canbank Factors sale done (₹14 crore cost, ~4x expected). Written-off pool ~₹18,000 crore and dwindling; recoveries exceed slippages each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: SMA position and LCR?
qa_highlights.answer: SMA 0–2 for ≥₹5 crore is 0.51% (₹7,043 crore); SMA 2 is 0.21% and SMA 1 0.09%. LCR 115% at 30 Sep 2026.

Bond yield path: management said yields could harden further, with HTM also subject to provisioning; a 44 bps hardening in Q2 drove the treasury swing.
Whether ECL provisions are passed on to customers: ROA could settle near 0.80% if not passed on, above 1% if passed through; no decision yet.
Gold loan competition from large NBFCs; management expects no yield pressure but acknowledged rising competition.
CASA at 29% vs 30–32% guidance; FCNR(B) leverage spread of only 40–50 bps to be offset from Q3, and the bulk deposit replacement may need to continue.

532488|2026-03.headline: Divi's Q4 FY26 consolidated PBT rose to ₹963 crores (vs ₹864 crores YoY) and PAT to ₹751 crores, while management guided only to "stable" margins.
532488|2026-03.overview: Divi's reported Q4 FY26 consolidated total income of ₹2,986 crores, PBT of ₹963 crores and PAT of ₹751 crores, including a ₹90 crore forex gain. For FY26, total income rose to ₹11,067 crores from ₹9,712 crores, PAT to ₹2,568 crores from ₹2,191 crores, after a one-time ₹74 crore Labour Code charge. Management said volumes in generics were stable with some pricing pressure, while West Asia-related disruption raised raw material, solvent and freight costs and forced some suppliers to declare force majeure. Management declined to quantify FY27 margins, guiding only to stable margins and double-digit revenue growth.

segments.name: Custom Synthesis (CS)
segments.commentary: FY26 product mix was 55% CS. Management cited a strong project pipeline across Phase II/III, validation and qualification stages; late life-cycle management volumes may decline as products mature.

segments.name: Peptides
segments.commentary: Several fragments validated in the quarter with more in pipeline; capabilities include protected amino acids, solid-phase and liquid-phase synthesis, and 3,000-litre SPPS capacity.

segments.name: Contrast media
segments.commentary: Iodine-based contrast media in commercial sales to innovators, supplied in multiple tonnes; Gadolinium compounds still at qualification as customers' products are in Phase II/III.

qa_highlights.question: Is the worst behind on raw material availability, and how is methanol sourcing being managed for H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the conflict affected only about one month of FY26 and there were no production stoppages, but sourcing is difficult across solvents and other materials; availability is being reviewed quarterly, with securing supply for the next 3 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 and the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a margin figure, saying it is difficult to project but expected to remain stable; capex for FY27 expected to be constant unless a major CS project emerges.

qa_highlights.question: Why was constant currency growth only about 6% despite capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Most capex was capitalised late in the year; management said it will now track reported revenue growth instead, citing currency volatility, and attributed slower growth to generic pricing pressure rather than a single product.

qa_highlights.question: What would it take to return to 38% margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said generic pricing pressure and higher material costs (rising again due to the war) are the key drags; a return to 38% depends on market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: How long from capex to revenue for the new long-term CS supply agreements?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for about 2 years but timelines range from 6 months to 3 years, depending on customer approvals and regulatory queries.

qa_highlights.question: How do the rupee depreciation and raw material and freight cost pressures net out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said currency gains help as the company is export-led, but a rupee reversal would also hurt; about 40% of raw material spend is imported, on total raw material spend of ₹4,000-5,000 crores against ₹11,000 crore revenue.

532488|2026-06.headline: Divi's Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose to ₹891 crores (from ₹557 crores), with Custom Synthesis at 60% of revenue and management guiding to double-digit growth.
532488|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income was ₹3,144 crores versus ₹2,529 crores a year earlier, and consolidated PAT was ₹902 crores versus ₹545 crores. Standalone revenue grew 10% in constant currency, with Custom Synthesis at 60% and Generics at 40% of revenue. Gross margin and inventory build were the main swing factors: the company stocked solvents and raw materials on a rolling three-month basis at higher cost and also built validation-batch inventory, and management said margins should be read on a full-year basis. Management declined to quantify commercial ramp-up timelines for the three capex projects, citing CDAs and regulatory timing.

financial_highlights.metric: Change in inventory (as cited on call)
financial_highlights.change: vs ₹50-100 crores run rate per analysts

segments.commentary: Contributed 60% of standalone revenue in Q1 FY27. Three major capex projects are in validation and about 70% of their combined ~₹2,000 crore cost has been capitalised. Management said the company has about 18 to 20 projects commercialised or being commercialised.

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Contributed 40% of standalone revenue. guidance_outlook: Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 and said it would show double-digit growth 'no matter what'; it did not give a specific gross or EBITDA margin figure.
Management said full-year gross margin is about 60% and EBITDA margin is similar to last year, but Q1 gross margin was about 68% and the company does not expect that level to persist.

qa_highlights.question: What is the typical ramp from validation quantities to commercial quantities for dedicated capex projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, citing CDAs and product-specific variability. Commercial volumes start only after validation, customer qualification and agency approval.

qa_highlights.question: Will the inventory build (≈₹500 crores change in inventory) normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is holding a rolling three-month stock of materials at higher cost to avoid production or shipment stoppages, and validation batches also add to inventory. Management said the inventory level depends on Middle East macro conditions and would fall if costs normalise.

qa_highlights.question: How should full-year margins compare with last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year gross margin is about 60% and EBITDA margin is similar to last year, with lumpiness by quarter. Q1 gross margin was about 68% and the next quarter may be higher or lower.

qa_highlights.question: Is solvent pricing softening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices were flat for a few weeks and then rose again depending on Middle East news. Supply is not always easily available, so the company is holding inventory three months ahead rather than just-in-time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Gadolinium contrast media project?
qa_highlights.answer: It is still in customer Phase II and III qualification and is on a slow track while the customer awaits regulatory approval. Validation has not yet been completed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any inventory gain in the gross margin line this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: No, management said there was no inventory gain recorded in Q1.

risks_watch: Solvent and raw material cost volatility tied to West Asia; prices can rise again within weeks, and the 3-month inventory policy ties up working capital (inventory ₹4,413 crores).

Gross margin normalisation after Q1's approximately 68% level, and the inventory-change swing from roughly ₹50-100 crores run rate to about ₹500 crores.
Net forex loss of ₹7 crores in Q1 versus a gain of ₹39 crores a year earlier; INR movements affect reported margins.
Freight and logistics disruption affecting export schedules, and the need to watch validation-to-commercial conversion for the Kakinada Unit 3 site.

532488|2026-09.headline: Divi's Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 64% YoY to ₹1,127 crore on total income of ₹3,770 crore, with management guiding only to double-digit revenue growth.
532488|2026-09.overview: Consolidated total income for Q2 FY27 rose about 32% YoY to ₹3,770 crore, with PBT up 65% to ₹1,505 crore and PAT up about 64% to ₹1,127 crore. For H1, total income was ₹6,907 crore (vs ₹5,389 crore) and PAT ₹2,029 crore (vs ₹1,234 crore). Net material consumption fell to about 32% of sales from 40%, attributed to Custom Synthesis mix, Unit 3 backward integration and cost benefits. Operating cash flow weakened, which management tied to a large capex cycle, with CWIP at ₹1,638 crore.

segments.name: Custom Synthesis (CS)
segments.commentary: Contributed 62% of standalone sales in H1; standalone revenue grew 17% YoY in constant currency for H1. Management said several programs are in validation or commercialization, with validation quantities supplied in Q2.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: H1 revenue ₹571 crore, up from ₹492 crore (about 16%). Management cited growing global demand for preventive healthcare and wellness ingredients.

segments.name: Peptides
segments.commentary: Management said several fragments are under validation or customer qualification; several 3,000 litre SPPS lines are being installed. Peptides are innovation-only, with no generic peptides at present.

Asset turn for the overall basket is about 1.5x; management declined to split asset turns by peptides vs small molecules.

Input costs rose on petrochemical solvents; ocean freight and air freight costs rose due to Red Sea/Suez and Middle East disruptions. Company holds rolling three-month inventory for critical materials.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was difficult to give a cumulative figure; around 60-70 projects are handled at any time across stages, and the three major investment projects are the only ones announced.
