532493|2026-03.headline: FY26 turnover of INR1,157 crores in line with guidance; order book INR2,141 crores standalone and FY27 top-line growth reaffirmed at 15-20%.
532493|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 turnover of INR1,157 crores, in line with the start-of-year guidance, with operating cash flow of INR370 crores versus minus INR99 crores a year earlier. Q4 billing was INR490 crores (up 16% YoY) and Q4 fresh orders were about INR530 crores, taking the standalone order book to INR2,141 crores at 31 March 2026. Management reaffirmed FY27 top-line growth of 15-20% and guided to roughly INR1,600 crores-plus of orders in FY27, with a board-approved in-principle demerger of the space, meteorology and hydrology business. The call leaned heavily on a long-range "near-triple turnover in 4.5-5.5 years" narrative, with proprietary IP products and the Su-30 upgrade positioned as upside rather than included in the numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margins sustain given rising space and export mix, and what are the exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are to wholly owned subsidiary ARC with higher value add (RF portion of SDRs co-developed with Rafael), with gross margin near 40-45%. Space subsystems for a defence satellite contributed decently in Q4 and similar orders are expected from ISRO and defence. Management said margins are a function of order mix and may vary.

qa_highlights.question: How much more capex is needed for the 3x revenue target, and will working capital improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR40-50 crores a year with no additional capex beyond normal run-rate. Working capital will rise with volumes but should be funded within sanctioned limits; receivables realisation is expected to continue, so finance cost should be similar to FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Given space order book share has shrunk, how does margin mix look?
qa_highlights.answer: Space is about 10-15% of sales, so a lower space order share should not hurt overall margins. Management said FY26 margin was about 55% and the aim is to sustain it, with guidance at the top end and margin numbers possibly slightly lower to avoid disappointment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MMIC dependency and sourcing position?
qa_highlights.answer: No issues encountered in MMIC production or development. Most active devices in subsystems are sourced from the in-house MMIC division, and the company is now promoting MMICs to domestic and international customers.

qa_highlights.question: Has the total addressable market (about INR28,000 crores FY26-FY28) changed?
qa_highlights.answer: The total accessible market is unchanged, but programme timing has slipped, so the opportunity window moves from FY28-FY29 to FY30-FY31 due to budget and priority delays.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and business scale for the Su-30 upgrade programmes?
qa_highlights.answer: Radar qualification likely in FY28 with user qualification about one more year; EW (Angad) development expected to complete in about one year; production orders are expected 2-3 years after that, with DRDO timing not controlled by Astra.

qa_highlights.question: Why was JV profit only about INR1 crore and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR1 crore figure was for Q4; full-year JV share of profit was about INR8 crores after tax. Around $2 million of forex provision and ongoing R&D weighed on profit. JV EBITDA is projected at 18-20%, implying at least about INR20 crores share of profit on INR600 crores revenue, with management calling INR20 crores a minimum.

532493|2026-06.headline: Astra Microwave won a ~Rs 2,205 crore HAL Uttam radar order, lifting order book to ~Rs 4,300 crore, while Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 182 crore.

Management attributed the quarter's weak revenue to delayed programs caused by inspection and specification-proof issues and supply-chain gaps, which it expects to recover in Q3 and Q4. The late-July receipt of the HAL Uttam radar order (about Rs 1,870 crore excluding GST, stated as Rs 2,205 crore including GST in the call) more than doubled the order book. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of about Rs 1,350 crore (plus or minus 25%) and said the space and weather businesses will be spun off as a separate listed entity from April 1, 2027.

532497|2026-06.headline: Radico Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 1,684 crore and EBITDA Rs 348 crore (20.7% margin, record); P&A volumes up 36%.

532497|2026-09.headline: Radico Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 1,746 crore and EBITDA margin 20.4%, with P&A volume up 36% and FY27 P&A volume guidance raised to 30%.
532497|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as the strongest quarter in company history, with IMFL volume above 10 million cases (+7% YoY), revenue of Rs 1,746 crore and EBITDA of Rs 356 crore at a 20.4% margin (+462 bps YoY). Prestige & Above (P&A) volume hit a record 5.28 million cases, up 36%, while the Regular category declined about 15% after the Andhra Pradesh route-to-market change and Maharashtra and Karnataka policy changes. Gross margin was 48.0%, up 440 bps YoY but down 109 bps QoQ, with packaging inflation costing about Rs 27 crore. The company upgraded FY27 P&A volume growth guidance to 30% and kept EBITDA margin guidance at around 20%. Leadership changes: Dilip Banthiya joined the Board as Executive Director and CFO, and Saket Somani was elevated to Deputy CFO.

segments.commentary: IMFL EBITDA margin is about 24%+ in Q2; non-IMFL margin is about 9.5-10%.

segments.commentary: FY26 turnover was Rs 475 crore; management says it is well on track for 25% value growth in FY27. Virasat Indian Single Malt is priced at about Rs 3,500-4,000 a bottle.

segments.commentary: Vodka reached 6.3% of IMFL in Q2, up from 3.7% in 2025 and 4.5% in 2026. Flavoured vodka is about 75% of Radico's vodka; vodka is about 30% of Radico's volume.

segments.commentary: Shipments to West Asia have recovered after the initial disruption in Feb-Mar 2026; freight costs are the main issue. Radico is now listed in 4 UK airports and in about 70 duty-free locations, with a target of 100.

532505|2026-03.headline: UCO Bank FY26 net profit rose 13.21% to Rs 2,768 crore; gross NPA fell to 2.17%, and FY27 guidance was held at 12-14% credit growth.

Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.17% (down 52 bps), net NPA at 0.27%, and PCR at 97.79%. segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Q4 treasury income was negative Rs 16 crore versus about Rs 130 crore in Q3, after a Rs 135 crore MTM hit on the AFS book. Management cited a Rs 848 crore treasury segment profit against Rs 557 crore, which it said it would clarify offline.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth 10-12%, credit growth 12-14% (unchanged on deposits, credit range held at 12-14%).
FY27 CASA 37-38%; RAM share raised to 62-65%; CD ratio 80-82%.

ROA of 0.87% in FY26; management expects 0.95-1% by end of FY27.
FY27 IT budget above Rs 1,000 crore, following Rs 899 crore spend in FY26.

532508|2026-06.headline: Jindal Stainless Q1 FY27: revenue up 10.5% YoY and PAT up 7.7%, but finished-goods volume fell 7.3% on gas shortages; FY27 volume guidance held.
532508|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was resilient on profit but weak on volume, as industrial gas (LPG/propane) shortages and Middle East logistics issues hit the first weeks of April 2026. Revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew 10.5%, 1.4% and 7.7% YoY, with management prioritising value-added mix and thinner grades. Consolidated net debt fell to INR 2,950 crore (net debt/EBITDA 0.53x). Management kept FY27 volume guidance (8-10% growth) and the INR 18,000-20,000/t H1 EBITDA guidance, deferring any revision to the next quarter. Indonesia melt shop (1.2 MTPA) has started ramping up; the Jindal Stainless Indonesia structure changed from subsidiary to associate effective 1 July 2026.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the balance sheet and capex timelines, but cautious and deferential on volume and margin, holding guidance until Q2 and evasive on June-July volumes, inventory and CBAM; analysts pushed on export sustainability and whether gas shortages cost volume and margin.

532508|2026-09.headline: JSL cut FY27 volume growth guidance to 4-6% (from 7-9%) but raised EBITDA/ton guidance to INR 20,000-22,000 after Q1 disruptions.
532508|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed a recovery from Q1 disruptions: finished goods sales volume rose 14% QoQ and 3% YoY, and consolidated revenue, EBITDA and PAT grew about 14%, 8% and 17% QoQ. Consolidated EBITDA was INR 2,762 crore (about 2% YoY) and PAT INR 1,666 crore (about 9% YoY). H1 FY27 deliveries were 1.25 million tons, down 2% YoY. Management cut full-year volume guidance but raised EBITDA per ton guidance, while flagging import pressure from China-origin 200-series products after the QCO suspension.

segments.name: Domestic market
segments.commentary: Domestic market grew 14% QoQ per management, but domestic volumes were flat to down ~1% YoY per analyst question; import pressure cited as cause. Key end-uses: automotive, railways, metros, lifts, elevators, white goods.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports grew 20% QoQ and 36% YoY, to 11% of Q2 volumes. Europe share fell as EU quota for duty-free supply was cut from ~12,000 tons to ~5,500-6,000 tons; growth came from North America, Korea, Japan, Middle East, Brazil and South Africa.

segments.name: Indonesia nickel (NPI/Weda Bay) and SMS
segments.commentary: Nickel operations remained EBITDA positive in Q2 and within management's USD 500-1,500/ton guidance range. Steel melt shop at IMIP is about to start commercial operations; no numbers given.

segments.name: Subsidiaries (Chromeni, Rathi, RVPL)
segments.commentary: Chromeni cold rolling utilisation about 85%, Rathi about 79%. Rabirun (RVPL) is used for polishing; cold rolling equipment there expected to be operational next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guidance revised to 4-6% from 7-9%; management says even the next two quarters will not reach the earlier range.
FY27 EBITDA per ton guidance raised to INR 20,000-22,000 from INR 18,000-20,000.
Capex guidance unchanged at INR 2,400-2,600 crore; net debt guidance unchanged at INR 2,500-2,800 crore.
Reiterated 3.5 million tons per annum sales volume target by FY29.
Implied H2 FY27 volume growth of about 10-14% YoY, per analyst calculation from the revised guidance.
HAPL line commissioning by end-2026 or start of 2027; some cold rolling mills under commissioning now. Maharashtra plan update deferred by another quarter or two due to slow land acquisition.
Anti-dumping duty decision expected by about 31 December 2026 per management hope; DGTR timeline extended to 28 March 2027.
capex_capacity: Q2 capex about INR 895 crore; FY27 YTD INR 1,555 crore, in line with guidance; all announced projects said to be on track.
Downstream expansions: 1.1 million ton HRAP and 0.17 million ton CRAP capacity; some cold rolling mills now commissioning; HAPL line commissioning expected by end-2026 or early 2027.
Maharashtra greenfield plan delayed by land acquisition; another one to two quarters before a clear plan.
Chromeni utilisation ~85%, Rathi ~79%; utilisation overall cited around 89-90% by analyst.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand described as healthy across automotive, railways, metros, lifts, elevators and white goods.

Imports surged after the QCO suspension (from April 2026); Chinese-origin imports in the first four months were nearly two-thirds of prior full-year imports. Management says the increase is mainly 200-series.
Management pursuing anti-dumping duty; industry representations to government on QCOs and ADD ongoing.
NSR fell about 6.5% QoQ per analyst; management attributed it to mix across 200/300/400 series, raw material price movement and market sentiment.
Raw material costs rose QoQ due to contract lag from higher nickel prices in Q1, per management.
Management said it does not hold inventory for stock-building.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in the implied H2 FY27 volume growth of 10-14% YoY, and how do domestic and exports split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said order book is not the constraint; supply depends on ramp-up of new downstream facilities. Without Q1 disruption, it would have been close to original guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What are the commercial terms of the JFE Steel technical assistance agreement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose the fee, describing it as payment for services. JFE is expected to help improve 400-series operations and quality.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 3.5 million ton FY29 target remain on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said long-term and FY29 volume plans, projects and capex remain intact and are not affected by quarterly movements.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q2 domestic volumes flat YoY and what is the capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 was normal, volume is affected by grade and thickness mix, and domestic vs export is a strategic balance. Analyst cited ~89-90% utilisation versus 95-100% historically.

qa_highlights.question: Is the tax benefit from the amalgamation quantifiable and what is its timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said brought-forward losses of INR 400-500 crore translate to about INR 100-125 crore tax benefit; NCLT approval typically takes about 12 months, so benefit likely in next or following fiscal year.

qa_highlights.question: Will rising gas and crude prices pressure other expenses and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sharp gas price moves would hit the industry in the short run but cost pass-through should normalise over time; it is planning for no sharp disruption.

risks_watch: Import pressure from China-origin 200-series products while QCO remains suspended until 28 March 2027; ADD decision timing uncertain.
H2 FY27 volume ramp to 10-14% YoY depends on commissioning of downstream capacity and no fresh industrial gas or logistics disruption.
Europe export quota cut; European share of exports has fallen materially.
Nickel price volatility affecting Indonesia nickel profitability; drought at IMIP industrial park.
Maharashtra greenfield project delayed by land acquisition.
Gas price increases could compress margins; EBITDA/ton raise requires margin recovery.
Limited disclosure at subsidiary level (Chromeni, Rathi, RVPL) pending amalgamation.
532508|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on long-term plans and FY29 target, but cautious and somewhat evasive on the Q2 domestic volume shortfall and on subsidiary-level profitability, deferring detail to IR follow-ups.
key_quotes: The second quarter marked a strong recovery from disruptions witnessed in Q1 of this year.
In this dynamic environment, JSL revises its full -year volume growth guidance to 4% to 6%, from earlier 7% to 9%
Inventory, we don't keep. We don't plan by building any stocks or anything, because in our kind of business, it doesn't make much sense.

Whereas IMIP is having that drought and when we were discussing with our partners, so they were expecting that if the rain doesn't come in the short term, they were -- they were also expecting that some disruption may come.

rows.why: HAPL line commissioning guided for end-2026 or early 2027, 1.1 mt HRAP under construction and 0.17 mt CRAP mills commissioning now, against utilisation of about 89% (analyst cited) versus 95-100% historically.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Maharashtra greenfield plan deferred by one to two quarters on slow land acquisition, so no clear new capex announcement is expected near term even with utilisation near 89-90%.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.why: FY27 volume guidance was already cut to 4-6% from 7-9%, management says the next two quarters will not reach the earlier range, and China-origin 200-series imports are pressuring domestic volumes (domestic flat to down ~1% YoY in Q2).

rows.when: by about 31 Dec 2026 per management hope; DGTR timeline exte
rows.why: Imports in the first four months after QCO suspension were nearly two-thirds of prior full-year imports; ADD would relieve 200-series pressure but timing is management hope, not a firm date.

rows.why: Brought-forward losses of INR 400-500 crore translate to about INR 100-125 crore tax benefit, with NCLT approval typically taking about 12 months.

rows.label: Export diversification beyond Europe
rows.why: Exports grew 20% QoQ and 36% YoY to 11% of Q2 volumes as EU duty-free quota was cut from about 12,000 t to 5,500-6,000 t, with growth from North America, Korea, Japan, Middle East, Brazil and South Africa.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY29 3.5 mt target, capex being on track and the EBITDA/ton raise, but cautious and evasive on the Q2 domestic volume shortfall, the JFE fee and subsidiary profitability; analysts pushed on the implied H2 ramp, utilisation and imports.

532509|2026-03.headline: Suprajit Q4 FY26: quarterly revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore, Q4 consolidated PBT ~INR 97 crore (almost double YoY); FY27 guide: double-digit growth, consolidated EBITDA margin 12-13.5%.
532509|2026-03.overview: Management reported that Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore on a quarterly run rate, with consolidated PBT of about INR 97 crore, almost double last year. Full-year revenue grew about 17% and EBITDA about 19-20%, helped by the SCS (ex-SES) turnaround, which turned EBITDA positive in Q4 at about +2% after roughly -20% in Q1. Standalone and ex-SCS growth was more modest (standalone revenue +7.1%, ex-SCS consolidated revenue +8.7%). Management guided to double-digit FY27 revenue growth and a 12-13.5% consolidated EBITDA margin, with GCM (including SCS) margins rising from about 6% to 10-12%.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated operational EBITDA, FY26 (ex-SCS basis as stated)
Surplus cash in mutual funds, March 2026

segments.name: SCD (Suprajit Controls Division, to be renamed GCM)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 10% and EBITDA margin crossed double digits for the first time at 11% for FY26. Mexico consolidated into Matamoros and Brownsville made main US warehouse; SAL India and Shanghai Lone Star each grew about 20%.

segments.name: DCD (Domestic Cable Division, to be renamed ICM)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 9%, dampened by YoY price concessions passed to customers; management says EBITDA margin was robust and unchanged for the year. Margin optics were weighed by STC and corporate overheads being allocated to DCD.

segments.name: PLD (Phoenix Lamps, to be renamed PLE)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell about 3% and EBITDA declined as commodity (moly, tungsten) increases were not fully passed on; margin down about 200 bps, with TRIFA brand sales hit by Middle East conflict. First orders executed for a large US retailer.

segments.name: SED (Suprajit Electronics Division, to be renamed for sensors, electronics and displays)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 20-30% (figures cited differently on the call) with EBITDA growing substantially; management expects double-digit margin in FY27 (about 10% currently). Digital clusters and electronic throttle controls driving momentum.

segments.name: SCS (Suprajit Components/SES, Europe and Morocco business)
segments.commentary: Turned EBITDA positive in Q4 (about +2%) after -20% in Q1, -6% in Q2 and -2% in Q3. Poland shut, manufacturing moved to Morocco (single shift), warehouse moved from Germany to Hungary, and tool room moved to Morocco; SCS will be folded into GCM from Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group revenue: double-digit growth expected.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 12% to 13.5%, inclusive of SCS.
GCM (SCD plus SCS): double-digit revenue growth; EBITDA margin expected to rise to 10-12% from about 6% in FY26.
ICM (India cables): double-digit revenue growth with stable EBITDA margin, citing market share gains, Beyond Cable ramp-ups, and insolvency of a large European halogen lamp maker.
FY27 capex about INR 200 crore: about INR 80 crore India, about INR 50 crore global, about INR 50 crore STC, about INR 15-16 crore corporate.
Margin guidance excludes the approximately $6 million Section 301 tariff recovery claim, which is pending in court; management expects it within 3-6 months if resolved.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex about INR 200 crore: land and building about INR 80 crore, plant and machinery about INR 105 crore, software and IT about INR 15 crore.

Electronics Division central building to be demolished and rebuilt as a three-storey facility over two years (about INR 30-40 crore total, about half in FY27); operations relocated to leased premises meanwhile.
SAL Chennai Plant-2 (Vallam) to be built for SAL captive capacity; SCD capacity expansion and SCD India Chennai expansion planned.
STC new building delayed, now expected to complete in Q3 FY27.
Morocco operating mainly on one shift, so management sees no capacity constraint there.
demand_pricing: Management attributes DCD revenue slowdown to YoY price cuts; underlying India volume growth said to be about 12-14% ex-PLD, ahead of industry (around 11% last year).

Pass-through: management expects most commodity cost increases to be recovered from customers; tariff recoveries from customers and US government ongoing, with US refund portal process causing timing lag.
Tariff leakage: unrecovered Mexico steel duties of about $1-2 million absorbed in FY26 P&L, expected to persist in material cost in FY27 and FY28.
Halogen lamp market: largest halogen lamp maker's insolvency is driving new low-cost sourcing enquiries to India; Indian OEMs with halogen tails already buying from PLD.

Electronics: throttles (ferrite-magnet based), digital clusters (Supra 1.0/2.0/2.5/3.0 platforms) and actuators (seat-lock, charging-gun) are new products; mostly two-wheeler today, with a North American off-highway cluster win starting this year.
China: supplying a large Chinese EV OEM with door lock and latch cables; around 20+ projects, 3-4 commercialised; management aspires to about 20% share of that customer's business in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 margin guidance at risk from Middle East-driven cost inflation, and what gives confidence on growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth confidence rests on already-won business that executes a year later; launch delays are the main risk. Management expects most commodity increases to be passed to customers and calls the forecast conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin dip in last two halves: is it tariff under-recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said some tariff recoveries are yet to happen and may be skewing the number; he would check the H1 vs H2 gross margin split. Management said unrecovered tariffs are charged off, so any recovery is upside.

qa_highlights.question: Break-up of INR 200 crore capex by division and Electronics Division allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: India about INR 80 crore, global about INR 50 crore, STC about INR 50 crore, corporate about INR 15-16 crore; Electronics building is INR 30-40 crore over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why are DCD and Phoenix Lamps margins down, and what recovers them?
qa_highlights.answer: DCD margin is strong; the drop reflects STC (about 150 staff vs 50-60 a year earlier) and corporate SAP/global costs allocated to DCD. PLD margin fell about 200 bps on flat top line and TRIFA/aftermarket softness; recovery expected from a US retailer, Indian aftermarket and European insolvency-driven demand.

qa_highlights.question: Does the SCS/GCM margin jump from 6% to 10-12% come from tariff recovery or operations?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly operational: restructuring at SCS and Controls, Juarez to Matamoros, Jiaxing stabilisation, and Europe relocation to Hungary/Morocco. Tariff recovery is a smaller contributor and the guidance excludes the $6 million Section 301 claim.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Mexico steel duty costs and the $6 million Section 301 claim affect FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Unrecovered Mexico duties of $1-2 million will be a permanent material cost. The $6 million Section 301 claim is excluded from guidance; resolution expected in 3-6 months.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict driving commodity and supply-chain cost inflation; recovery from customers is assumed but not assured.
Customer launch timing slips could delay the double-digit growth guidance.
Unrecovered Mexico steel tariffs of about $1-2 million a year become a permanent material cost.
Timing of US tariff refunds and the pending $6 million Section 301 recovery; both are court and portal dependent.
Phoenix Lamps margin recovery depends on the US retailer ramp and aftermarket revival; halogen tail declines slowly.
Electronics margin guidance is only for one year; FY28+ unclear.
Management declined to give a China share number explicitly; China aspiration of about 20% of one customer's business is unproven.
532509|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the SCS turnaround and FY27 margin path, but hedged repeatedly on Middle East, commodity and launch-timing risks. Evasive on quantifying the FY26 tariff charge, the Q3-Q4 gross margin dip and the order book; detailed on capex and division renaming.

I think the heavy lifting of the significant restructuring is all behind us. Hence, the outlook is good.
Our margin guidance is without considering that, yes.

rows.why: STC new building expected to complete in Q3 FY27 and SAL Chennai Plant-2 and SCD India Chennai expansion are planned, but no volumes or utilisation figures were given, and Morocco runs mostly on one shift, so capacity need is not evidenced.

rows.why: Management guides double-digit FY27 group revenue growth and India underlying volume growth of about 12-14% ex-PLD, although DCD revenue grew only about 9% on price cuts and PLD revenue fell about 3%.

rows.why: FY27 capex of about INR 200 crore is already allocated, and utilisation is described only as mostly one shift, so no new capex announcement is signalled beyond the planned SCD and SAL expansions.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management calls its forecast conservative and the $6 million Section 301 tariff recovery, excluded from guidance, could land within 3-6 months, but the timing depends on court and portal outcomes.

rows.why: Middle East-driven commodity inflation and customer launch slips could delay double-digit growth and the 12-13.5% margin, and management hedged on both repeatedly.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Electronics products (digital clusters on Supra 1.0-3.0 platforms, throttles, actuators) are ramping, with a North American off-highway cluster win starting this year, and PLD has first orders executed for a large US retailer.

rows.label: China EV OEM door lock/latch cables
rows.why: Around 20+ projects with 3-4 commercialised, and management aspires to about 20% share of that customer's business in 2-3 years, but declined to give a share number and the aspiration is unproven.

rows.label: Halogen lamp low-cost sourcing shift to India
rows.why: The largest halogen lamp maker's insolvency is driving new low-cost sourcing enquiries to India, and Indian OEMs with halogen tails already buy from PLD, though the halogen tail declines slowly.

rows.label: Commodity pass-through and tariff recovery
rows.why: Management expects most commodity cost increases (moly, tungsten) to be recovered from customers, but PLD margin fell about 200 bps as they were not fully passed on and US refunds are subject to a portal lag.

tone.note: Management was confident on the SCS turnaround (Q4 EBITDA about +2%) and the FY27 12-13.5% margin path, but hedged on Middle East commodity inflation, launch timing and the FY26 tariff charge; analysts pressed on the Q3-Q4 gross margin dip, tariff recovery and the DCD/PLD margin decline.

532509|2026-06.headline: Suprajit Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% to INR1,070 crore and operational EBITDA 57% to INR129 crore, while standalone EBITDA was flat at INR60 crore.
532509|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR1,070 crore (up 24% YoY) and operational EBITDA reached INR129 crore (up 57%). Global Cables and Mechatronics (GCM) drove the gain, with EBITDA margin rising from 5.8% to 12.6% after the global restructuring. Standalone margins were squeezed by raw material and wage inflation in ICM (margin ~15% to ~13%) and by delayed price pass-through in PLE (margin 6.7%, down 2.8pp); management calls both timing issues and expects recovery in Q2-Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance from the 25 May 2026 release.

financial_highlights.change: invested in mutual funds and bonds

segments.name: Global Cables and Mechatronics (GCM, formerly SCD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~27-28% reported, ~23% after adjusting for two months of SCS Canada/China tranche not in base; EBITDA margin 12.6% vs 5.8%. Management says 12%-plus is current, guidance 10%-12% retained.

segments.name: India Cables and Mechatronics (ICM, formerly DCD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~21%, broad-based across OEM and aftermarket; EBITDA up 4.2% with margin down from ~15% to ~13% on raw material and wage costs. CBS revenue up 110% and brake shoes/pads up ~80% off a small base.

segments.name: Phoenix Lighting and Electricals (PLE, formerly PLD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 5.4%, EBITDA down 45%, margin 6.7% (down 2.8pp) on delayed aftermarket price increases; new prices now in effect. Ramp-up with a large US retailer; Middle East Trifa sales soft.

segments.name: Sensors, Electronics and Displays (SED)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 48%, EBITDA up 100%, margins close to double digits, led by digital clusters and electronic throttle grips. July was reported as the division's highest-sales month.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance from 25 May 2026 release reiterated: consolidated double-digit revenue growth; consolidated operational EBITDA margin 12%-13.5%.
GCM: double-digit growth and 10%-12% operational EBITDA margin (current margin is above this range).
ICM: EBITDA margin around last year's ~15%; PLE: around 12%; SED: around 10%, in line with last year.
Management expects standalone margin shortfall to recover by Q2-Q3; on full year, standalone margin within ~50bps of last year, with at most ~100bps downside as an extreme case.
Management said it will not change margin guidance until year-end, after the restructuring outcome is visible.
GCM expects strong double-digit growth in Q2 based on July trends; August is a seasonally weak month.
capex_capacity: SED: capacity expansion on a war footing; company is relocating out of current site for about six months into a larger leased premises, then rebuilding the plant as a multistorey electronics facility. Earlier plan was sized for about INR250 crore of business.
New STC R&D building on track for completion in Q3 FY27.

GCM: new product launches in China (one of the largest Chinese EV OEMs, about 25 cable projects won, 5-6 launched) and India (lines for a large US OEM building a resilient supply chain). Business wins across India, Mexico and China.
SED: about six launches in the plant this month and next, across instrument clusters, actuators/sensors and throttle position sensors.
US retailer PLE programme: store count expected to roughly triple or go 4x next year.
demand_pricing: Indian automotive sector grew about 22% in the quarter; passenger vehicle and 2-wheeler both grew at double digits per management.
Global automotive and non-automotive demand described as flat to muted; GCM growth attributed to new contract wins replacing lost business.
Pass-through: raw material increases largely recovered; wage increases (mainly northern region) being negotiated, with some customers agreeing and others still resisting.

Three large GCM contract wins announced about a month earlier: largest EV cable contract (USD 5m annual, USD 37m lifetime); European luxury OEM (USD 2m a year, USD 12m lifetime); Japanese OEM (USD 1.2m a year, USD 6m lifetime).
Management described the business as very competitive globally but consolidating, which may favour stronger players on margin.
Braking: CBS customers include TVS and HMSI; management says validation cycles are long for this safety-critical product.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-offs or FX benefits in GCM margin, and is 12% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no material one-offs; margin gains came from restructuring, leaner operations, cost projects and top-line growth. It is at 12%-plus, but guidance of 10%-12% is retained and depends on product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Can SCS be disclosed separately for Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No. SCS was disclosed separately only until March 2026; it is now folded into GCM as entities were merged or restructured.

qa_highlights.question: Was the GCM 27% growth flattered by FX or acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reported 27% overstates growth; excluding April-May from the second SCS tranche, growth is about 23%. The USD/INR rate has been stable at about INR95-96 over the period.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Last year's gains came from large favourable currency moves on loans, debtors/creditors and forward covers, plus a Morocco subsidy not repeated. Currency has been stable since March, so the Q1 figure is much smaller.

qa_highlights.question: What drives SED growth and the EV exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is in instrument clusters, actuators/sensors and TPS, across multiple customers, with ICE as well as EV demand. Mahindra throttle ramp-up used a rare-earth-free design. Management expects strong growth for at least 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin shortfall in ICM/PLE temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a timing issue: price pass-through is still being negotiated, with recovery expected in Q2 and Q3 and cost reduction under way.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for PLE run-rate and the European insolvency?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes are declining in the old business; the European insolvency is unresolved. Management expects more clarity in the next quarter and sees opportunities over three to six months, with US retailer business growing.

risks_watch: Standalone margin recovery in ICM and PLE depends on customers accepting wage and raw material pass-through; management said some customers are still resisting wage increases, mainly in the northern region, with recovery expected in Q2-Q3.
GCM margin of 12%-plus is above the 10%-12% guidance band; management said it will not revise margin guidance until year-end after the restructuring outcome is visible, and August is seasonally weak.
PLE volumes in the legacy business are declining and the European insolvency remains unresolved; management expects clarity over the next quarter and an opportunity over three to six months.

SED capacity: relocation out of the current site for about six months and rebuild as a multistorey facility, with the earlier plan sized for about INR250 crore of business; execution and interim disruption to watch.

Other income fell sharply YoY because prior-year currency gains and a Morocco subsidy did not repeat; the Q1 base is much smaller, and the GCM growth rate is partly flattered by reported (not constant currency) figures, with the 27% reported growth about 23% after excluding the second SCS tranche.
key_quotes: Consolidated revenue grew up by about 24%. EBITDA was up by nearly 57%.
In operational result, there is no. Operational performance…
I don't think there is any concern on meeting the guidance that we have already set out.
So what I'm saying is that the order inflows are pretty strong .
So it's impossible to put a target there.

More cautious on standalone ICM and PLE margins, which it attributes to timing, and it declined to give a separate SCS disclosure, a median price per unit, or a content-per-vehicle target.

532509|2026-09.headline: Suprajit H1 FY27 consolidated revenue up 22% to INR2,205 crore and EBITDA up 40% to INR267 crore; H1 margin 12.1%.

Management said Q2 showed margin recovery at ICM and PLE after Q1 pricing pressure, and GCM margin rose from 7.4% to 10%+ as restructuring completed. Standalone H1 revenue grew 18% to INR1,034 crore while standalone EBITDA grew only 3% to INR149 crore. Management guided H2 consolidated margin slightly above H1, conditional on commodity prices and the Middle East conflict, while SED margins remain under pressure from component cost inflation and pricing negotiations.

532513|2026-03.headline: TVS Electronics Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin rose to 5.96% (+413 bps YoY) on revenue of about Rs 117 crore, while FY26 revenue grew only about 6%.
532513|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was about Rs 117 crore, up 2% YoY and 3% QoQ, with EBITDA of about Rs 7 crore and PAT of about Rs 3 crore. Management said pricing is a lever but is being held back to protect CNG volume growth, and capex is being maintained at about INR1,700-1,800 crore for FY27.

FY27 capex is guided at about INR 9,000 crore, mainly the petchem project, and the dividend is to be maintained.

Net debt has fallen to about $1.1 billion from more than $1.5 billion in March 2025, and interest cost savings of about Rs70-75 crore per quarter are now in the P&L.

segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR774 crore, up YoY, with EBITDA of INR64 crore (8% margin) versus INR7 crore a year ago. H1 revenue grew 15% YoY and H1 EBITDA was INR120 crore against a loss of INR28 crore in H1 FY26.

segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR833 crore, up 13% QoQ, with EBITDA INR175 crore (20% margin vs 15% in Q1). H1 revenue INR1,569 crore and EBITDA INR291 crore; FY27 remains a transition year due to reduced demand from a large biologics client.

The board has lifted its pause on the PFS divestment, with the route and advisers still to be decided by a board committee.

qa_highlights.question: Why did rebate income decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Discoms are now paying early and capturing rebates themselves, while PTC pays generators early and then recovers from Discoms later, so PTC's net rebate income fell.

qa_highlights.question: Why was a Rs 17.4 crore provision booked (Note 8)?
qa_highlights.answer: It relates to a generator's claim from a legal dispute over a contract. The adjudicating authority ruled that PTC pay first and recover later. The provision was made on auditor consultation, with no clear visibility on recovery from the counterparty.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash position and who are the top debtors?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone net cash was Rs 2,451 crore at 30 June, before the interim dividend. Top debtors: Punjab (about Rs 860 crore), UP (about Rs 600 crore), Haryana (about Rs 500 crore), Rajasthan (about Rs 400 crore), and Tamil Nadu (about Rs 300 crore). Management said PTC's own exposure is not more than 60 days, as back-to-back pass-through items inflate gross debtors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for PFS and how much stake will PTC keep?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a transaction advisor (SBI Capital) is appointed and the process is under way. No stake or timeline was committed, and the structure depends on advisor input.

qa_highlights.question: Will CERC's HPX rule affect PTC?
qa_highlights.answer: The CERC rule caps shareholding at 5% for trading members. PTC holds more than 22% of HPX, so it cannot be a trading member unless it reduces its stake below 5%, which management said depends on several factors.

risks_watch: Lower net surcharge and rebate income: management attributes it to improved Discom liquidity and early Discom payments, and called the cyclicality uncertain; no split of surcharge between long-term and short-term sources was given, with data promised by email.

Receivables: gross debtors of Rs 4,469 crore at 30 June, with Punjab (about Rs 860 crore), UP (about Rs 600 crore) and Haryana (about Rs 500 crore) as the largest; management says PTC's own exposure is not more than 60 days, but back-to-back items inflate the figure.
Rs 17.4 crore provision (Note 8) for a generator's legal claim; recovery from the counterparty is not assured and may lead to further litigation.
Long-term book and volumes: long-term volume fell YoY on lower hydro generation; no new long-term contracts expected in FY27 or FY28; average remaining PPA tenor not disclosed.
Timing risk on new capacity: Teesta Urja (1.2 GW) first power around December 2026 at 40%-50% initially; NTPC Green 1,200 MW PPA around FY29; battery storage still in discussion with no tie-up.

PFS disinvestment: transaction advisor (SBI Capital) appointed; no stake, structure or timeline committed beyond 'closer to end of FY27'. HPX: PTC holds more than 22% and cannot be a trading member unless it cuts below 5%.
key_quotes: Obviously, this kind of dividend, 23 rupees per share, cannot be sustained or should not be expected every year.
Nothing is likely to expire in next three years.
But as far as the PTC exposure is concerned, so that is not more than, I will say not more than 60 days wherein PTC has taken an exposure and that is pending.
So, we are not expecting to add any long-term contracts in that duration.

532524|2026-09.headline: PTC India Q2 FY27 standalone PAT fell 15% to Rs 113 crore on 24% higher volume, as net surcharge income dropped from Rs 42 crore to Rs 26 crore.
532524|2026-09.overview: Trading volume rose 24% YoY to 32.5 billion units in Q2 and 18% to 58.2 billion units in H1, led by exchange and medium-term trades. Operating income was flat-to-down (Rs 134 crore vs Rs 137 crore), while PBT fell 15% to Rs 152 crore as net surcharge and treasury income declined after a special dividend reduced cash balances. Consolidated PAT fell 28% to Rs 159 crore, with a Rs 51 crore impairment provision at PTC Financial Services (PFS) a major drag. Management said PFS stake sale is in process with a transaction advisor appointed, but gave no timeline.

segments.name: Power trading (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q2 volume 32.5 bn units (+24%); H1 58.2 bn units (+18%), with 60% of H1 volume on exchanges. Q2 trading margins: short-term 0.69 paise/unit, medium-term 3.17, cross-border 6.98, long-term 7.98.

segments.name: Cross-border trade
segments.commentary: Flows to Bangladesh stable with regular payments; Bhutan 1,200 MW winter supply contract signed; Nepal import/export commenced. Lower cross-border income reduced operating income in Q2 as margin is higher than exchange trades.

segments.name: HPX (Hindustan Power Exchange, 22.5% stake)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 18.13 crore vs Rs 9.89 crore YoY; H1 revenue Rs 32.11 crore vs Rs 22.18 crore.

segments.name: PTC Financial Services (PFS)
segments.commentary: Q2 impairment provision of Rs 51 crore vs a Rs 57 crore reversal in Q2 FY26; management cited a roughly Rs 40 crore reduction in PFS PAT, which flowed into consolidated numbers.

guidance_outlook: No volume guidance given for Q3 or full year; management said there is no dramatic change in the current situation.

PFS stake sale: transaction advisor appointed, information dossiers being prepared, nodal officers appointed in PFS; no deadline or dates announced, citing regulatory approvals (RBI, SEBI if required).
Management expects power prices to stay firm in peak hours; intraday price range cited from under Rs 1 to Rs 10 per unit; storage additions expected over the next 12-18 months.
Minerals exchange: planned launch with initial focus on five minerals including iron ore; investment described as modest and funded from cash; partnerships under evaluation.
Dividend: company practice is to declare dividends once a year; no interim dividend expected soon.
Joint venture with NLC: board has met and a business plan is being formulated; near-term (1-2 years) business activity expected to be limited due to connectivity lead times of 3-4 years.
capex_capacity: Solar PPA of 1,200 MW signed with NTPC Renewable Energy in the last quarter.
Floated a 500 MW / 2,000 MWh tender for long-term renewable-linked power procurement.
Bhutan winter supply contract of 1,200 MW signed.
Contracted supply to NG delayed by NG itself; safeguards in contract mean no commercial impact, but power has not yet been delivered.
Minerals exchange and NLC JV are early-stage; no capacity or capex figures disclosed.
demand_pricing: Total generation grew 10.64% in H1 while PTC trading volume grew over 18%, which management cited as evidence of market share gains.
Net surcharge income fell from Rs 42 crore to about Rs 26 crore YoY, as DISCOMs paid on time and PTC reduced outstanding dues from a large state utility.
Treasury income fell after a special dividend paid out of the PEL divestment proceeds reduced cash.
Rebate income is netted within sale and purchase account, not shown separately in P&L; management said it depends on DISCOM liquidity.
Gas-based power costs have risen sharply due to Middle East conflict, affecting trading partners' behaviour and RE project timelines.
Market coupling remains pending regulatory directives; HPX competitiveness depends on it.
Minerals trading competitors cited as MSTC and Mjunction.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timeline of the PFS stake sale, and is there a deadline?
qa_highlights.answer: Process is on track with a transaction advisor appointed; no deadline or specific dates given because of regulatory approvals and the aim to realise good value after operational stabilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone PAT fall despite higher operating income, and which expense items rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Net surcharge fell from Rs 42 crore to about Rs 26 crore and treasury income fell after the special dividend; establishment costs rose about Rs 2 crore on a base of about Rs 10 crore due to staff transfer from PEL.

qa_highlights.question: What are the trading margins by category?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 margins: short-term 0.69 paise/unit, medium-term 3.17, cross-border 6.98, long-term 7.98; overall about 2.89 paise/unit.

qa_highlights.question: How is rebate income generated and where is it reported?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebate is earned when a DISCOM does not avail rebate while PTC pays generators early; it is netted within sale and purchase account, not a separate P&L line.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost double QoQ despite large cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Includes working capital interest (about Rs 14 crore in H1, Rs 7 crore in Q2) and surcharge expenses paid back-to-back against surcharge income booked in other income.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PTC entering mineral trading and what are the regulatory and competitive issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Synergy with existing 500-600 C&I clients and mining customers; regulator is Indian Bureau of Mines; competitors are MSTC and Mjunction; partnerships being considered.

qa_highlights.question: Can HPX trade given the 5% exchange-trader cap while PTC holds 22.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: PTC does not trade on HPX; trading would require cutting its stake from 22.5% to 5%, a decision still under evaluation.

risks_watch: PFS stake sale: no timeline, and shareholder concerns about the process being delayed or halted; PFS stock trades near 50% of book value per a shareholder question.
Consolidated earnings are exposed to PFS provisions (Rs 51 crore impairment in Q2).
Lower surcharge and treasury income and reliance on rebate income, which depends on DISCOM liquidity.
Recoverability of a previously written-off amount depends on judicial process with no timeline.
Market coupling regulatory directives still awaited; HPX volume outlook depends on it.
Minerals exchange and NLC JV: execution timing uncertain, with connectivity lead times of 3-4 years.
532524|2026-09.management_tone: Management was confident on volume growth and cash strength but defensive on PFS divestment, repeatedly declining to give dates or timelines and rejecting shareholder suspicions. Profit decline was attributed to PFS provisions and lower surcharge and treasury income, which management framed as improved receivables management.
key_quotes: Our risk management is far more composed and should that lead to some reduction in the rebate income, still it is much more sustainable than anything else.
The revenue and the trading margin is only a by-product of that, but for some quarters it may go down, for some quarters it may go up.
To divest like a slump sale is not a wise thing. It will not be good for the PTC shareholders also.
There is absolutely no intent on the part of the management to stop in between or create this smoke screen.

532525|2026-03.headline: Bank of Maharashtra FY26: net profit INR7,019 crore (+27% YoY), full-year NIM 3.91%, ROA 1.86%, all guidance met; FY27 ROA guidance 1.80%.
532525|2026-03.overview: Management reported that all FY26 guidance metrics were met, several with headroom, with total business up 17% and advances up 22% YoY. Gross NPA fell 29 bps to 1.45% and net NPA to 0.13%, while operating profit rose 16% to INR10,826 crore. Management created an INR200 crore "global geopolitical uncertainties" provision in Q4 as a buffer against the West Asia crisis, and said stress is not yet visible in MSME. Non-interest income was weak (2.51% growth) due to a one-time INR290 crore MTM hit from the RRB amalgamation. FY27 guidance was issued across 18-19 parameters, with ROA lifted to 1.80%.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail grew 32% YoY; home loans +29%, vehicle loans +56%, gold loans +53% to INR24,000 crore, of which about INR5,000 crore is co-lent with NBFCs. Retail slippages in Q4 were about INR100 crore.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book grew 22% YoY, with RAM split 63:37 (retail/agri/MSME vs corporate). Corporate reported no slippages in Q4; INR72,000 crore sanctioned in FY26 with INR34,500 crore undisbursed.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME grew 11% YoY (about INR6,000 crore added per management); MSME NPA fell to 1.54%. Q4 MSME slippages were about INR400 crore.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri grew 13% YoY; agri NPA was 7.72% (about INR3,100 crore). Q4 agri slippages were about INR300 crore.

segments.name: GIFT City IBU
segments.commentary: Overseas advances rose to INR6,142 crore from INR3,517 crore (2% of book). Management said the IBU turned profitable in March after covering all overheads; 650 million USD booked against a 1 billion USD 12-month aspiration.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: AFS reserve swung from +INR175 crore in Q3 to -INR362 crore at 31 March; FVTPL MTM gain of about INR40-45 crore booked.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total business growth 16-17%; advances 18%; deposits 14-15%; CASA around 50%.
RAM growth 18% with RAM corporate mix at 60:40 (+/-2%); non-interest income growth 10%; NII growth 15%.
FY27 NIM guidance 3.75%; cost to income below 40%; ROA 1.80%; ROE 20% or more.
GNPA within 2%, NNPA within 0.25%, slippage below 1%, credit cost around 1%, PCR around 98%, CRAR maintained at 18%.
Management expects FY27 tax at about 10% of PBT (OP tax rate 13-14%), with PBT-basis tax about 18-20%, after unabsorbed losses of about INR1,200-1,300 crore were used up in Q1.
Debt waiver: about INR2,000 crore expected (INR917 crore overdue + INR1,067 crore NPA eligible KCC accounts), with approval expected Q2 to Q3 FY27; agri NPA could fall to about 5.33%.
capex_capacity: Project 321: 321 new branches in the first 3-year phase, 183 functional to date; Board has approved 1,000 branches over 5 years.
GIFT City IBU: first business booked September 2025; retail products planned for H2 FY27.
PLI for Scale 4 and above not yet released; 100% provision made, release pending discussions.
demand_pricing: Management expects West Asia crisis impact to show from Q2 FY27 rather than Q1, with Brent above USD115 cited as a risk; no MSME stress seen as of March.
Q4 SMA-1 was INR241 crore and SMA-2 INR56 crore as of 31 March (per analyst).
Management said it would price risk more carefully where risk rises, but gave no specific pricing action.
Pool/assignment book of about INR14,000 crore is largely lent to AA/AAA NBFCs; security cover is low as it is pool-based.
Gold co-lending slowed after RBI's CLM1 guidelines from 1 January 2026; fresh underwriting resumed in early March, with 9 NBFC co-lending partners signed.

qa_highlights.question: How will the West Asia war affect corporate and MSME accounts from April onward, and what stress is visible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no stress was visible in March and MSME NPA fell to 1.54%, but impact is expected from Q2 FY27 and depends on how long the crisis lasts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the special provision fall to INR1,010 crore from INR1,200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the COVID buffer was released, and a new INR200 crore global geopolitical uncertainties provision was built in Q4, with no regulatory prescription behind it.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the one-time non-interest income drag?
qa_highlights.answer: A one-time INR290 crore MTM provision was taken on investments in the RRB (Vidharbha Konkan Gramin Bank) that was amalgamated into a single Maharashtra RRB, with the bank as sponsor.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net worth fall QoQ and gold loans drop about 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Net worth fell due to AFS reserve movement and dividends (interim 10% plus final 12%, about INR1,692 crore total). Gold loans dropped because fresh underwriting paused during the shift from CLM2 to CLM1 co-lending; underwriting resumed in early March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the bank is on the normal tax rate from Q2 FY26, with OP tax at 13-14%. FY27 PBT-basis tax is expected around 18-20%, and the call gave a 10% figure for the tax on PBT in the same answer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment split of Q4 slippages?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail about INR100 crore, agri about INR300 crore, MSME about INR400 crore, and corporate nil.

risks_watch: West Asia / crude-driven stress in MSME and corporate books from Q2 FY27; a 1.2% to 2% geopolitical provision top-up is open.
Timing and size of the state KCC debt waiver (about INR2,000 crore); the scheme is not yet approved.
Tax-rate normalisation to about 25% creates an earnings headwind; management guided FY27 PBT-basis tax at 18-20%, but the figures given on the call are inconsistent.
Non-interest income growth (2.51% in FY26) versus 10% target; a fee-income push is planned for FY27.
Gold co-lending volume recovery after CLM1 transition; the book fell about 17% QoQ.
Pending PLI payout for Scale 4 and above, and the NCLT recovery pipeline (about INR7,500 crore in NCLT).
532525|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and FY27 guidance, with management calling the targets "sacrosanct". Cautious and somewhat evasive on the West Asia impact, saying the full effect cannot yet be gauged and that the crisis is not over.
key_quotes: we have been able to meet all the guidance and at some of the places with a decent margin above the guidance that was shared in the beginning of the year.
These are sacrosanct numbers for us. We will be achieving itself.
So we can only hope that the crisis resolves and what damage must have happened, the impact, how fast it can be replaced is also needs to be seen.

532525|2026-06.headline: Bank of Maharashtra Q1 FY27: net profit up 27% YoY to INR2,020 crore, advances up 27%, NIM 3.85%, all guidance parameters beaten.
532525|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 2026) with total business up 19% YoY, advances up 27% and deposits up 13%, against guidance of 16-17%, 18% and 14% respectively. Operating profit rose 21% YoY to INR3,117 crore and net profit rose 27% to INR2,020 crore. Asset quality held: gross NPA flat QoQ at 1.45%, net NPA 0.13%, credit cost 0.99%. Management kept its FY27 guidance unchanged despite the faster growth, and flagged the NIM (3.85%, down 10 bps YoY) and the rising cost of deposits QoQ as the points to watch.

financial_highlights.value: INR1,04,000 crore added in past year

financial_highlights.change: Guidance 14%; no CDs raised in Q1
vs INR33 crore in March quarter; includes one-time SR of INR104 crore

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 25% YoY; retail gross NPA 0.34% per management, with home loan sanctions in the past 12 months 80% from CIBIL 750+ borrowers.

segments.name: Agri
segments.commentary: Agri advances grew 30% YoY; agri gross NPA 7.58%, down from about 9% a couple of quarters back.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 23% YoY; MSME gross NPA 1.60%, and MSME gross NPA rose QoQ.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew about 30% YoY, up from 17-18% in the prior four quarters; RAM:corporate mix at 63:37.

segments.name: IBU (GIFT City)

Gold loans about INR13,000 crore, up 75% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NII (14.5%) lag advances growth (27%), and would management revisit the 18% loan growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management kept NII guidance of 15% and NIM of 3.75%, citing a branch-level profitability dashboard and tighter pricing. It said it would keep the 18% advances guidance, with IBU contributing 3 points of the 27% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did current account balances fall sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it not a major concern: the decline is about 2,500-3,000 bps of the current account book, and CASA still grew 9% YoY, adding INR14,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Agri provisions and debt waiver impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Eligible portfolio INR3,500 crore; government receivable INR2,750 crore; maximum haircut INR450-500 crore, already covered by INR1,700 crore of provisions. Settlement expected within FY27, plus INR50,000 per farmer incentive into SB accounts.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the tax rate lower?

qa_highlights.question: Opex growth of 8-9% vs balance sheet growth above 20%?

qa_highlights.question: Why did treasury profit jump to INR266 crore and what is the outlook?

ECL provisioning of about INR125 crore per quarter through March 2031 against net worth.

532525|2026-09.headline: Bank of Maharashtra Q2 FY27: business up 25% YoY, advances up 30%, ROE 26.98%, GNPA down 47 bps to 1.25%.
532525|2026-09.overview: Management said all FY27 guidance metrics were met in Q2, with business crossing INR7 lakh crore and advances growing 30% YoY (23% ex-IBU). Operating profit rose 31% and net profit 41% YoY, lifting ROE 440 bps to 26.98% and NIM 12 bps to 3.97%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 1.25% and NNPA at 0.12%, helped by write-off recoveries and lower NPA provisions, while INR500 crore of ECL provisions was booked in the standard asset line. Cost of deposits fell 4 bps YoY to 4.38%, though management acknowledged a QoQ rise tied to FCNR(B) and OFCB raises of about $1.65 billion.

financial_highlights.metric: Cost of deposits / cost of funds

segments.name: Advances / large credit
segments.commentary: Large credit up 38% YoY to INR36,000 crore, of which INR18,000 crore from GIFT City IBU and INR18,000 crore domestic (19% growth). Domestic credit ex-IBU grew 23%, with RAM, retail, agri and MSME each above 20%.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Deposits up 22% YoY, or 19% ex-FCNR(B); CASA up 12% YoY with INR19,000 crore CASA added over the last FY.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri book INR44,000 crore, up 34% YoY (about INR11,000 crore). Agri gold loans INR18,600 crore vs INR6,500 crore in Sep-25; agri stress down 35 bps to 3.51%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Total gold loan outstanding INR33,000 crore; MSME gold loan about INR2,000 crore. Retail gold declined QoQ as loans were reclassified to agri/MSME under RBI norms.

guidance_outlook: Management said all FY27 guidance metrics across growth, profitability, asset quality and capital were met in H1.
Domestic credit guidance is 18%; management sees no challenge sustaining above 18% with INR23,000 crore pipeline and INR10,000 crore expected to be disbursed by March 2027.
Recovery target from written-off accounts of INR1,300-1,500 crore annually for the next 4-5 years; FY27 recovery so far INR1,023 crore.
ECL: total assessed requirement INR2,500 crore over 4 years; INR750 crore already provided (INR250 crore earlier plus INR500 crore in Q2), which management says covers more than 1 year.
Maharashtra debt-waiver government receivable (about INR2,700 crore of eligible INR3,500 crore): about INR1,200 crore received to 30 Sep; SLBC timeline for balance is 31 March 2027.
capex_capacity: Branch expansion: about 200 branches planned annually; 77 branches made functional in H1 FY27.
Employee strength raised to 17,500 from about 13,000 two years earlier, driven by branch expansion and specialist hiring (treasury, IBU, IT).
IT budget: INR900 crore in FY25 and INR985 crore in FY26, with a large share on cyber security.
Pipeline sector mix: infra power about 18%, roads/HAM about 12%, renewables about 10%, metals and others about 10%; data centres cited as a niche growth area.
demand_pricing: Credit growth ex-IBU of 23% YoY; IBU book INR18,500 crore funded partly by about $560 million of FCNR(B) leverage. The FCNR(B) special window has closed.
Repricing: management raised rates on several MCLR-linked state PSU facilities (several thousand crore, about 25 bps on some) in Q1, contributing to NIM gains.
Global yield on advances 8.86%, domestic 9.02%; IBU yield not disclosed on the call.
Gold loan pricing tiers: agri lowest, MSME about 50 bps higher, non-priority retail highest.
EBLR-linked loans are 47% of the loan book.

qa_highlights.question: Provisioning: standard/restructured provisions rose to INR603 crore from INR76 crore; what is the ECL preparedness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NPA provisions fell from INR580 crore a year ago to INR120 crore this quarter, helped by recoveries. Standard-asset provisions rose to INR603 crore including INR500 crore of ECL; total ECL assessed at INR2,500 crore over 4 years, with INR750 crore already provided.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit growth sustain after the FCNR window closes, and will write-off recoveries continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IBU leverage was about $560 million from FCNR(B) and the window is closed; domestic growth is 23% and the INR23,000 crore pipeline supports growth above the 18% guidance. Write-off recovery target is INR1,300-1,500 crore a year for 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FCNR(B) is fixed at 6.51%, OFCB at 6.11%, and 1-year CDs at about 7.75-7.9%. About $1.65 billion was raised via FCNR(B) and OFCB against a $1.5 billion plan, with 5-year fixed-cost borrowings and a 3x oversubscribed MTN issue; YoY cost of deposits fell 4 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the 30 bps QoQ rise in yield on advances despite IBU mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to repricing of MCLR-linked state PSU accounts (about 25 bps on several thousand crore), a one-off write-off recovery impact of about 2-3 bps on NIM, and a 3-4 bps ITR refund. Only INR30 crore of the INR125 crore recovery has gone to interest income so far.

qa_highlights.question: Drought exposure and restructuring under SLBC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no visible agri stress; special SLBC restructuring applies at 33-50% crop loss (1-year moratorium, up to 3-year tenor) and above 50% loss (5-year tenor including 1-year moratorium). Farmer applications open till February 2027; past experience suggests 10-15% take-up, with about 5% provisioning on the restructured amount.

qa_highlights.question: Agri gold and retail gold trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri gold loans rose to INR18,600 crore from INR6,500 crore YoY. Retail gold declined QoQ because loans were reclassified to MSME/agri under RBI norms; total gold outstanding INR33,000 crore and MSME gold about INR2,000 crore.

risks_watch: Drought and El Nino: Maharashtra drought could trigger SLBC restructuring; management estimates 10-15% take-up and says no visible stress yet.
ECL transition: INR2,500 crore total assessed; management said the number may fall; surplus provisions of INR1,600-1,800 crore (COVID, global uncertainties INR200 crore) can be used.
Cost of deposits: QoQ increase from high-cost FCNR(B)/OFCB/CD raises; FY28 impact on margin depends on deployment.
Maharashtra debt-waiver balance of about INR1,500 crore receivable; management does not count on it and timing depends on state process (deadline 31 March 2027).
Pace of IBU growth after the FCNR(B) window closed; IBU yield not disclosed.
Cyber and DPDP compliance; management deferred detailed answer.

rows.why: About INR1,200 crore of eligible INR3,500 crore (about INR2,700 crore eligible) received to 30 Sep, with about INR1,500 crore balance; SLBC timeline is 31 March 2027 and management does not count on it.

532527|2026-03.headline: Ramkrishna Forgings Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 1,216.78 crore, with EBITDA margin at 17.1%, and management guides to further improvement in FY27.
532527|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 1,216.78 crore, up 28% YoY and 11% QoQ, with EBITDA excluding other income of Rs 208.19 crore (up 111% YoY, 27% QoQ) and margin of 17.1%. Profit before tax was Rs 64.33 crore, held back by about Rs 10.4 crore of consolidation effects (Rs 5.9 crore subsidiary profit elimination and Rs 4.5 crore Mexico subsidiary loss). FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 4,238 crore (up 5%) and EBITDA Rs 642.70 crore (up 15%), while PBT fell 24% to Rs 112.58 crore versus Rs 148.79 crore (excluding exceptional items) in FY25. Q4 orders won totalled Rs 594 crore over four years, split 56% automotive and 44% non-automotive.

+111% YoY vs Rs 98.5 crore; +27% QoQ vs Rs 163.37 crore
Up about 220 bps QoQ (stated as 'almost 2 20 basis points', read as ~220 bps)
+117% QoQ vs Rs 29.69 crore in Q3 FY26
+5% YoY vs Rs 4,034 crore in FY25

segments.commentary: Forging utilisation about 70% in Q4 FY26 versus 83% in Q4 FY25, per the analyst's reading of the presentation; management attributes the gap partly to the 8,000-ton press line added. Cold forging utilisation is about 40%, held back by slow global PV approvals; management hopes for 75-80% by FY26 year-end (FY27 per the call's context).

segments.commentary: Capacity is 62,000 tons (cited as 78,000 tons by one analyst, with about 70,000 tons referenced by management); production was 26,000 tons in FY26 and sales are lower due to machining mix. Management expects 85-90% utilisation over the year and margins of about 15-16%, with Rs 400-500 crore of incremental revenue from the new March-end capacity.

segments.name: Aluminium forgings
segments.commentary: Post commissioning, bulk supplies have started to EV equipment makers globally; management cites margins of about 14-15%, with commodity realisation near Rs 400/kg.

segments.name: Railway wheelsets (JV)
segments.commentary: Rail wheel JV expected to start production by Q1 FY27, with 230,000-wheel capacity and a railway offtake guarantee of about 40,000 wheels in FY27 for revenue of roughly Rs 400-450 crore.

segments.name: Trailer axles
segments.commentary: Revenue of about Rs 120 crore in FY26; management targets about Rs 250 crore in FY27 and a 10% market share.

guidance_outlook: Revenue: no FY27 number given; management expects 'healthy growth' on current order book and capacity. Analyst cited a prior 10-15% CAGR upper limit for FY27-28, and management declined to confirm it.
EBITDA margin: management expects continued improvement, with 100-150 bps better margin at around 80% utilisation if energy price increases are passed on.
Utilisation: overall capacity utilisation targeted at about 80% in FY27, roughly 350,000 tons of forging and casting; press plant around 85% by FY27 year-end.
Debt: reduction of at least Rs 400-500 crore in FY27, supported by promoter funding and operating performance.
Capex: FY27 capex limited to about Rs 400 crore at most, mainly JV contribution (about Rs 50 crore still to be paid) and value-add; no FY28 capex frozen yet.
Export mix: management expects exports to rise above 40% of volumes within about two years (from a historical 40:60 export:domestic split), with exports more remunerative.
Titanium/stainless aerospace alloys: order book reflection expected by FY26 year-end, but revenue not expected before FY29.
capex_capacity: Rail wheel JV: commercial production to start immediately after commissioning, around end-May/June 2026; 300 trial wheels to be submitted in June/July 2026.
Forging press line: 8,000-ton press added; press plant utilisation targeted at about 85% by FY27 year-end.
Casting: about 62,000-ton capacity, 26,000 tons produced in FY26; new capacity added by end-March 2026 is expected to generate Rs 400-500 crore of revenue in coming years.
Standalone casting business began commercial production on 31 March 2026, so nil standalone revenue in FY26.
Ring rolling running at 121% utilisation; no plans to add ring rolling capacity in FY27.
demand_pricing: North America Class 8 demand is strong; destocking in North American warehouses over the last three months, with fresh revenue expected from Q1 FY27; management expects this to last to about Q3 CY27.

Q4 orders of Rs 594 crore (four-year program): Rs 334 crore auto (Rs 323 crore CV, of which more than 50% export; Rs 11 crore EV) and Rs 258 crore energy (energy storage, North America) plus Rs 2 crore off-highway.

Pricing is pass-through: steel is passed on quarterly with a one-quarter lag; gas and other consumables are negotiated yearly. Management is seeking compensation for geopolitical energy cost increases via force majeure, with talks at an advanced stage.

Realisation: management attributed the lower realisation versus Q4 FY25 to lower raw material prices and cited a better product mix in H2 FY26; the analyst cited export realisation rising from Rs 1.77 lakh to Rs 1.85 lakh per ton.
Shipping costs up 15-20% and transit times up 15-20 days; floating inventory said to be in line. No West Asia revenue or exposure.
Domestic auto demand was strong after the September GST rate cut, with M&HCV, tractors and PVs reporting double-digit wholesale growth in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs 1,550 crore FY27 order book include castings, and what casting volumes and revenue are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: The figure covers forgings and castings together. Management expects 85-90% casting utilisation over the year, with margins of about 15-16% and Rs 400-500 crore of additional revenue. Management declined to put a figure on the incremental revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 debt and capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is to be reduced by at least Rs 400-500 crore in FY27. Capex is capped at about Rs 400 crore, mostly JV equity and value-add, with about Rs 50 crore of JV equity still to be paid.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and revenue growth in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue number was given, but management expects healthy growth. The EBITDA margin should keep improving, and at about 80% utilisation it could be 100-150 bps above the Q4 level if energy cost increases are passed on.

qa_highlights.question: How much did trailer axles contribute, and what are the targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue was about Rs 120 crore in FY26 at a 4-5% market share. The FY27 target is about Rs 250 crore at about 10% share.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wheelset JV's contribution and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Production starts by Q1 FY27 and about 40,000 wheels are expected in FY27 under the railway offtake guarantee, for revenue of roughly Rs 400-450 crore. Pricing is still being reset for two years of inflation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing for aerospace/titanium revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders should start reflecting in the order book by FY26 year-end, but revenue is not expected before FY29 given 12-24 month lead times and approvals.

532527|2026-06.headline: Ramkrishna Forgings Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 1,217 crore (+19.8% YoY), PAT Rs 46.9 crore (~4x YoY), EBITDA margin 17.96%.

532527|2026-09.headline: Ramkrishna Forgings Q2 FY27 revenue rose 54.9% YoY to Rs 1,405 crore, with EBITDA margin at 18.23% and PAT of Rs 71 crore.
532527|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached Rs 1,405 crore in Q2 FY27, up 54.9% YoY and 15.5% QoQ, with EBITDA (excluding other income) of Rs 256 crore and margin of 18.23% versus 13.5% a year ago and 17.96% in Q1. PBT was Rs 95 crore against a loss of Rs 10 crore last year, and PAT was Rs 71 crore, up 47% QoQ. Order wins of Rs 673 crore were booked, 52% from exports, with Rs 447 crore from castings, including a new North American light-vehicle casting programme. Management reiterated FY27 debt reduction of Rs 500 crore and ROCE of 12-15% by year-end, while declining to give FY28 guidance beyond a strong outlook for the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: Why has FY27 capex risen and how much is left?

qa_highlights.question: Power and shipping cost trends and margin path?

532528|2026-06.headline: Datamatics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore, with EBITDA margin up 343 bps to 19.7%.
532528|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 9.9% YoY to INR 513.9 crore and EBITDA rose to INR 101.1 crore at a 19.7% margin, with the margin gain attributed to cost discipline and operational excellence. Digital Operations drove growth (revenue up 16.1%, EBIT margin 19.3%), while Digital Technologies grew 6.1% at an 8.9% EBIT margin and Digital Experiences declined 5.3%. Management reiterated high single-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance, citing softness from geopolitical uncertainty, and said about 60% of FY27 deals won were AI-led or AI-driven. The TNQTech integration into Lumina Datamatics was completed in the quarter, and a INR 200 crore TNQTech payout was made in Q1.

qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to traction in KAi underwriting, KAiSDLC and KAiBRE, with legacy modernisation projects starting. It said the segment carries the AI investment, so removing it would give a much healthier margin.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not compete much with large listed IT players. Competition comes from funded local AI start-ups, GCCs and in-house tech teams.

qa_highlights.question: What are the risks to the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Key risks are customers automating in-house instead of outsourcing, captive/GCC setups, and geopolitical softness.
